title.zh: 卷一百二十二 志第七十五 禮二十五
title.raw: 卷一百二十二 志第七十五 禮二十五 Volume 122 Treatises 75: Rites 25

sentences.zh: 山陵、諡祔、服紀、葬儀與士庶之喪制為凶禮。

translations.literal: Mountain tombs, posthumous titles and enshrinement, mourning-garment regulations, burial rites, and the mourning regulations for scholar-officials and commoners constitute the rites of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial mausoleums, posthumous titles and enshrinement, regulations for mourning dress, burial ceremonies, and the mourning codes for officials and commoners all belong to the category of funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 其上陵忌日，漢儀如吉祭。

translations.literal: As for visits to the mausoleum on the anniversary of death, Han ritual treated them like auspicious sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Visits to the imperial tombs on death anniversaries were handled under Han practice much like regular auspicious sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宋制，是日禁屠殺，設素饌，輟樂舉哭，素服行事，因以類附焉。

translations.literal: Under Song regulations, on that day slaughter was forbidden, plain food was set out, music was stopped and weeping observed, and plain dress was worn in conducting affairs; it was therefore grouped by category accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song system, on those days slaughter was banned, plain vegetarian fare was served, music ceased and mourning cries were observed, and participants wore unadorned dress; these observances were accordingly classified with related funeral practices.

sentences.zh: 太祖建國，號僖祖曰欽陵，順祖曰康陵，翼祖曰定陵，宣祖曰安陵。

translations.literal: When the Taizu founded the state, he styled the Exalted Ancestor's tomb the Qin Mausoleum, the Shun Ancestor's the Kang Mausoleum, the Yi Ancestor's the Ding Mausoleum, and the Xuan Ancestor's the An Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu established the dynasty, he named the tombs of the Exalted, Shun, Yi, and Xuan Ancestors respectively Qin, Kang, Ding, and An Mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 安陵在京城東南隅，乾德初，改卜河南府鞏縣西南四十里訾鄉鄧封村。

translations.literal: The An Mausoleum was in the southeastern corner of the capital; at the beginning of Qiande, it was relocated to Dengfeng Village in Zi Township, forty li southwest of Gong County in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The An Mausoleum originally stood in the southeast corner of the capital; in early Qiande it was moved to Dengfeng Village in Zi Township, forty li southwest of Gong County in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以司徒范質為改卜安陵使，學士竇儀禮儀使，中丞劉溫叟儀仗使，樞密直學士薛居正鹵簿使，太宗時尹開封，為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi, Minister over the Masses, was made commissioner for relocating the An Mausoleum; Academician Dou Yi, ritual commissioner; Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou, ceremonial guard commissioner; Hanlin Academician Xue Juzheng, insignia commissioner; and the future Taizong, then prefect of Kaifeng, bridge-and-route provisioning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi, Minister over the Masses, was appointed commissioner to relocate the An Mausoleum; Dou Yi served as ritual commissioner, Liu Wensou as guard-of-honor commissioner, Xue Juzheng as insignia commissioner, and the future Taizong, then prefect of Kaifeng, as commissioner for bridges, roads, and relay supplies.

sentences.zh: 質尋免相，乙太宗兼轄五使事，修奉新陵。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi was soon removed from the chancellorship, and on the second day of the month the Taizong was additionally assigned to oversee the affairs of all five commissioners and to build and tend the new mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi was soon dismissed as chief minister, and on the following day Taizong was put in charge of all five commissioner posts to oversee construction of the new tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇堂下深五十七尺，高三十九尺，陵台三層，正方，下層每面長九十尺。

translations.literal: The imperial chamber below was fifty-seven feet deep and thirty-nine feet high; the tomb terrace had three tiers, square, each side of the lowest tier ninety feet long.
translations.idiomatic: The underground imperial chamber was fifty-seven feet deep and thirty-nine feet high; the tomb platform rose in three square tiers, each face of the lowest tier measuring ninety feet.

sentences.zh: 南神門至乳台、乳台至鵲台皆九十五步。

translations.literal: From the southern spirit gate to the breast terrace, and from the breast terrace to the magpie terrace, were each ninety-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: It was ninety-five paces from the southern spirit gate to the breast terrace, and another ninety-five paces from the breast terrace to the magpie terrace.

sentences.zh: 乳台高二十五尺，鵲台增四尺。

translations.literal: The breast terrace was twenty-five feet high; the magpie terrace was four feet higher.
translations.idiomatic: The breast terrace stood twenty-five feet high; the magpie terrace was four feet taller still.

sentences.zh: 神牆高九尺五寸，環四百六十步，各置神門、角闕。

translations.literal: The spirit wall was nine feet five inches high, encircling four hundred sixty paces, with spirit gates and corner towers set at each point.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit wall stood nine feet five inches high and ran four hundred sixty paces around the compound, with spirit gates and corner towers placed at the appropriate points.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「改卜陵寢，宣祖合用哀冊及文班官各撰歌辭二首。

translations.literal: The responsible officials stated: "For the relocation of the mausoleum chamber, the Xuan Ancestor should use the mourning register, and each civil-rank official should compose two hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "For relocating the mausoleum, the Xuan Ancestor should receive the mourning register, and each civil official in the procession should compose two dirges.

sentences.zh: 吉仗用大駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The auspicious procession should use the great imperial insignia guard.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious funeral procession should employ the full grand imperial guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 凶仗用大升輿、龍輴、鵝茸纛、魂車、香輿、銘旌、哀諡冊寶車、方相、買道車、白幰弩、素信幡、錢山輿、黃白紙帳、暖帳、夏帳、千味台盤、衣輿、拂纛、明器輿、漆梓宮、夷衾、儀槨、素翣、包牲、倉瓶、五穀輿、瓷甒、辟惡車。

translations.literal: The mourning procession should use the great carrying palanquin, dragon hearse, goose-down banner, soul carriage, incense carriage, inscribed banner, mourning posthumous-title register and seal carriage, exorcist figure, road-purchasing carriage, white-canopied crossbows, plain trust banners, money-mountain carriage, yellow and white paper canopies, warm canopy, summer canopy, thousand-flavor terrace trays, garment carriage, whisk banner, spirit-object carriage, lacquered catalpa coffin, barbarian coverlet, ceremonial outer coffin, plain feather fans, wrapped sacrificial animals, storehouse jars, five-grain carriage, porcelain jars, and evil-averting carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning train was to include the great carrying litter, dragon hearse, goose-down standard, soul carriage, incense carriage, inscribed mourning banner, carriage for the mourning register and posthumous seal, exorcist figure, road-purchasing carriage, white-canopied crossbows, plain trust pennants, money-mountain litter, yellow and white paper canopies, warm and summer canopies, trays of a thousand delicacies, garment litter, whisk standard, spirit-goods litter, lacquered catalpa inner coffin, barbarian coverlet, ceremonial outer coffin, plain feather fans, wrapped sacrificial offerings, storehouse vessels, five-grain litter, porcelain jars, and evil-averting carriage.

sentences.zh: 進玄宮有鐵帳覆梓宮，藉以棕櫚褥，鐵盆、鐵山用然漆燈。

translations.literal: Upon entering the deep chamber there was an iron canopy covering the catalpa coffin, spread with palm-fiber mats; iron basins and iron mountains were used to burn lacquer lamps.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the burial chamber an iron canopy covered the catalpa coffin, which rested on palm-fiber bedding; iron basins and iron mountains held burning lacquer lamps.

sentences.zh: 宣祖袞冕，昭憲皇后花釵、翬衣，贈玉。

translations.literal: The Xuan Ancestor wore the nine-symbol robe and crown; the Zhaoxian Empress wore flowered hairpins and pheasant-pattern robes, with jade bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan Ancestor was arrayed in full imperial robes and crown; the Zhaoxian Empress in flowered hairpins and pheasant-embroidered robes, with jade gifts added.

sentences.zh: 十二神、當壙、當野、祖明、祖思、地軸及留陵刻漏等，並制如儀。」

translations.literal: The twelve spirits, tomb guardians, field guardians, Ancestor Bright, Ancestor Thought, Earth Axis, and the clepsydra left at the mausoleum, among others—all were regulated according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The twelve spirit figures, tomb and field guardians, Ancestor Bright, Ancestor Thought, Earth Axis, and the water clock left at the tomb, among other items, were all arranged according to prescribed ritual."

sentences.zh: 有司又言：「按《儀禮》'改葬緦'注云：'臣為君，子為父，妻為夫也，必服緦者，親見屍柩，不可以無服，緦三月而除之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials further stated: "According to the Ceremonies and Rites, the commentary on 'reburial in finest mourning' says: 'When a subject acts for a lord, a son for a father, or a wife for a husband, they must wear finest mourning because they have personally seen the corpse and coffin and cannot go without mourning dress; finest mourning is removed after three months.
translations.idiomatic: The offices added: "The Ceremonies and Rites commentary on 'reburial in finest mourning' explains that when a subject serves a lord, a son a father, or a wife a husband, they must wear finest mourning because they have seen the remains in the coffin and cannot go unclad; finest mourning is worn for three months and then removed.

sentences.zh: '又《五禮精義》云：'改葬無祖奠，蓋祖奠設于柩車之前以為行始，至於改葬，告遷而已。

translations.literal: 'The Essentials of the Five Rites also says: 'Reburial has no ancestor-offering; for the ancestor-offering is set before the bier carriage as the beginning of the journey, whereas in reburial one merely announces the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: The Essentials of the Five Rites also notes that reburial omits the ancestor-offering, since that rite is performed before the bier carriage at the start of a funeral procession, whereas a reburial requires only an announcement of relocation.

sentences.zh: '今請皇帝服緦，皇親及文武官護送靈駕者亦服緦，既葬而除。

translations.literal: We now request that the emperor wear finest mourning, and that imperial kinsmen and civil and military officials escorting the spirit carriage also wear finest mourning, to be removed once burial is complete.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask that the emperor wear finest mourning, and that imperial relatives and civil and military officials escorting the spirit carriage do the same, removing it once the burial is finished.

sentences.zh: 不設祖奠，止於陵所行一虞之祭。

translations.literal: No ancestor-offering should be set up; only a single yu offering should be performed at the mausoleum site.
translations.idiomatic: No ancestor-offering should be held; only a single yu sacrifice should be performed at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 宣祖諡冊、諡寶舊藏廟室，合遷置陵內。

translations.literal: The Xuan Ancestor's posthumous-title register and seal, formerly stored in the temple chamber, should be transferred and placed inside the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan Ancestor's posthumous register and seal, previously kept in the ancestral temple, should be moved into the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 改葬之禮，與始葬同，几筵宜新，明器壞者改作。

translations.literal: The rites of reburial are the same as initial burial; spirit tables and mats should be new, and damaged spirit objects should be remade.
translations.idiomatic: Reburial rites follow the same procedures as an initial burial; offering tables and mats should be new, and any damaged burial goods should be replaced.

sentences.zh: 凡斂衣、斂物並易之。

translations.literal: All shrouding garments and shrouding objects should be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: All garments and objects placed in the coffin should be renewed.

sentences.zh: 其皇堂贈玉、鎮圭、劍佩、旒冕、玉寶，並以瑉玉、藥玉，綬以青錦。

translations.literal: The jade gifts, stabilizing scepter, sword and pendant, tasseled crown, and jade seals for the imperial chamber should all be of min jade and medicinal jade, with cords of blue brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The jade gifts, stabilizing scepter, sword and pendant set, tasseled crown, and jade seals for the burial chamber should all be made of min and medicinal jade, with blue brocade cords.

sentences.zh: 安陵中玉圭、劍佩、玉寶等皆用於闐玉。

translations.literal: In the An Mausoleum the jade scepter, sword and pendant, jade seals, and the like all used Khotan jade.
translations.idiomatic: At the An Mausoleum the jade scepter, sword and pendant, and jade seals had all been of Khotan jade.

sentences.zh: 孝明、孝惠陵內用瑉玉、藥玉。

translations.literal: Within the Xiaoming and Xiaohui mausoleums min jade and medicinal jade were used.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaoming and Xiaohui tombs had used min and medicinal jade instead.

sentences.zh: 啟故安陵，奉安宣祖、昭憲孝惠二後梓官於幄殿。

translations.literal: The old An Mausoleum was opened, and the catalpa coffins of the Xuan Ancestor and the two empresses Zhaoxian and Xiaohui were respectfully placed in the draped hall.
translations.idiomatic: Workers opened the old An Mausoleum and installed the catalpa coffins of the Xuan Ancestor and the Zhaoxian and Xiaohui empresses in the draped mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 靈駕發引，所過州府縣鎮，長吏令佐素服出城奉迎並辭，皆哭。

translations.literal: When the spirit carriage set out, at every prefecture, district, county, and market town along the route the chief officials and aides, in plain dress, went out of the city to welcome and take leave, all weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit carriage departed, magistrates and their deputies at every prefecture, county, and market town along the route came out in plain dress to receive and bid farewell to the procession, all in tears.

sentences.zh: 自發引至揜皇堂，皆廢朝，禁京城音樂。」

translations.literal: From the setting out until the sealing of the imperial chamber, court audiences were all suspended and music in the capital was forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: From the departure until the imperial chamber was sealed, court sessions were suspended and music was banned throughout the capital."

sentences.zh: 順祖、翼祖皆葬幽州，至真宗始命營奉二陵，遂以一品禮葬河南縣。

translations.literal: The Shun and Yi Ancestors had both been buried in Youzhou; only under Zhenzong were orders first given to build and tend their two mausoleums, and they were then buried in Henan County with first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Shun and Yi Ancestors had originally been buried in Youzhou; Zhenzong was the first to order construction of their two tombs, and they were interred in Henan County with first-rank funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 制度比安陵減五分之一，石作減三分之一，尋改上定陵名曰靖陵。

translations.literal: The regulations were one-fifth less than those of the An Mausoleum, stone work one-third less; soon the upper Ding Mausoleum was renamed the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The scale was reduced by one-fifth compared with the An Mausoleum and stone work by one-third; shortly afterward the upper Ding Mausoleum was renamed the Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年十月二十日，太祖崩，遺詔：「以日易月，皇帝三日而聽政，十三日小祥，二十七日大祥。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Kaibao, Taizu died; his testamentary edict stated: "Substitute days for months; the emperor shall hear government after three days, observe lesser mourning rites on the thirteenth day, and greater mourning rites on the twenty-seventh day.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the tenth month in the ninth year of Kaibao, Taizu died. His final edict read: "Count days as months: the emperor shall resume governance after three days, observe lesser mourning on the thirteenth day, and greater mourning on the twenty-seventh.

sentences.zh: 諸道節度防禦團練使、刺史、知州等不得輒離任赴闕。

translations.literal: Military commissioners, defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, acting prefects, and the like of all circuits must not leave their posts without permission to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commissioners, defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, and acting prefects must not leave their posts without authorization to come to court.

sentences.zh: 諸州軍府臨三日釋服。」

translations.literal: All prefectures, armies, and prefectural offices shall observe three days of mourning dress before releasing it."
translations.idiomatic: All prefectures, garrisons, and local offices shall observe three days of mourning before laying aside mourning dress."

sentences.zh: 群臣敘班殿庭，宰臣宣制發哀畢，太宗即位，號哭見群臣。

translations.literal: The ministers formed ranks in the palace courtyard; the chief ministers proclaimed the edict and concluded the mourning announcement; Taizong ascended the throne, wailing as he met the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers formed ranks in the palace courtyard. After the chief ministers proclaimed the edict and concluded the mourning announcement, Taizong took the throne and, wailing, received the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 群臣稱賀，復奉慰盡哀而退。

translations.literal: The ministers offered congratulations, then again paid respects of condolence, wept their fill, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers offered congratulations, then returned to pay condolences, wept their fill, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「群臣當服布斜巾、四腳，直領布衤蘭，腰絰。

translations.literal: The ritual officials stated: "The ministers should wear hemp mourning headcloths with slanting bands and four corners, straight-collared hemp mourning shirts, and waist mourning cords.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers reported: "Ministers should wear hemp mourning headcloths with slanting bands and four corners, straight-collared hemp mourning shirts, and waist mourning cords.

sentences.zh: 命婦布帕首、裙、帔。

translations.literal: Commissioned women should wear hemp mourning kerchiefs, skirts, and shawls.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned women should wear hemp mourning kerchiefs, skirts, and shawls.

sentences.zh: 皇弟、皇子、文武二品以上，加布冠、斜巾、帽，首絰，大袖、裙、褲，竹杖。

translations.literal: Imperial younger brothers, imperial sons, and civil and military officials of the second rank and above should add hemp mourning caps, slanting bands, hats, head mourning cords, large sleeves, skirts, trousers, and bamboo staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial brothers, imperial sons, and civil and military officials of the second rank and above should additionally wear hemp mourning caps, slanting bands, hats, head cords, wide sleeves, skirts, trousers, and carry bamboo staffs.

sentences.zh: 士民縞素，婦人素縵。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners wore white hemp; women wore plain unpatterned white.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners wore white hemp; women wore plain unpatterned mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 諸軍就屯營三日哭。」

translations.literal: All armies at their encampments observed three days of weeping."
translations.idiomatic: All armies at their encampments observed three days of mourning cries."

sentences.zh: 群臣屢請聽政，始禦長春殿。

translations.literal: The ministers repeatedly requested that he hear government; he first took the throne at the Changchun Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated requests from the ministers that he resume governance, he first held court at the Changchun Hall.

sentences.zh: 群臣喪服就列，帝去杖、絰，服斜巾、垂帽，捲簾視事。

translations.literal: The ministers took their places in mourning dress; the emperor removed staff and mourning cords, wore slanting band and hanging cap, rolled up the curtain, and attended to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers took their places in mourning dress. The emperor set aside his staff and mourning cords, wore a slanting headband and hanging cap, rolled up the curtain, and began to conduct state business.

sentences.zh: 小祥，改服布四腳、直領布衤蘭，腰絰，布褲，二品以上官亦如之。

translations.literal: At lesser mourning rites, he changed to hemp four-cornered cap, straight-collared hemp mourning shirt, waist mourning cord, and hemp trousers; officials of the second rank and above did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At lesser mourning he changed to a four-cornered hemp cap, straight-collared hemp shirt, waist cord, and hemp trousers; officials of the second rank and above followed suit.

sentences.zh: 大祥，帝服素紗軟腳折上巾、淺黃衫、緅皮鞓黑銀帶。

translations.literal: At greater mourning rites, the emperor wore plain gauze soft-foot folded-up cap, pale yellow robe, and dark purple leather belt with black silver fittings.
translations.idiomatic: At greater mourning the emperor wore a plain gauze soft-foot folded cap, pale yellow robe, and dark purple leather belt with black silver fittings.

sentences.zh: 群臣及軍校以上，皆本色慘服、鐵帶，靴、笏。

translations.literal: Ministers and military officers of company-commander rank and above all wore their regular colors in subdued dress, iron belts, boots, and tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and military officers of company-commander rank and above all wore their regular colors in subdued dress, with iron belts, boots, and court tablets.

sentences.zh: 諸王入內服衰，出則服慘。

translations.literal: The imperial princes wore full mourning when inside, and subdued dress when outside.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes wore full mourning dress inside the palace and subdued dress when they went out.

sentences.zh: 又成服後，群臣朝晡臨三日。

translations.literal: Furthermore, after assuming mourning dress, the ministers attended morning and evening for three days.
translations.idiomatic: After assuming full mourning dress, the ministers attended morning and evening audiences for three days.

sentences.zh: 大小祥、禫除、朔望，皆入臨奉慰。

translations.literal: At lesser and greater mourning rites, removal of mourning, and new and full moon, they all entered to attend and offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: At lesser and greater mourning, removal of mourning, and on new- and full-moon days, they all came in to attend and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 內出遺留物頒賜諸臣親王，遣使賚賜方鎮。

translations.literal: Objects left behind from within were distributed and bestowed on the various ministers and imperial princes; envoys were dispatched to present gifts to the frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Personal effects left behind were distributed among ministers and imperial princes, and envoys were sent to present gifts to the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，命宰臣撰陵名、哀冊文。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, the chief ministers were ordered to compose the mausoleum name and mourning register text.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day the chief ministers were ordered to compose the mausoleum name and the mourning register text.

sentences.zh: 明年三月十七日，群臣奉諡號冊寶告於南郊，明日，讀於靈坐前。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the third month of the following year, the ministers presented the posthumous title register and seal to announce at the southern suburb; the next day it was read before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the third month the following year, the ministers presented the posthumous title register and seal for announcement at the southern suburb; the next day it was read before the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 四月十日，啟欑宮，帝與群臣皆服如初喪。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the fourth month, the encoffining palace was opened; the emperor and ministers all wore dress as at the first mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the fourth month the encoffining hall was opened; the emperor and ministers all wore dress as at the initial mourning.

sentences.zh: 群臣朝晡臨殿中，退，易常服出宮城。

translations.literal: The ministers attended morning and evening in the central hall; upon withdrawal they changed to regular dress and left the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers attended morning and evening in the central hall, then changed to regular dress and left the palace precinct when they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十三日，發引，帝衰服，啟奠哭，群臣入臨，升梓宮于龍輴。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day the procession set out; the emperor in full mourning dress performed the opening offering and wept; the ministers entered to attend; the catalpa coffin was raised onto the dragon hearse.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day the funeral procession set out. The emperor, in full mourning, performed the opening offering and wept; the ministers came in to attend; and the catalpa coffin was lifted onto the dragon hearse.

sentences.zh: 祖奠徹，設次明德門外，行遣奠禮，讀哀冊，帝哭盡哀，再拜辭，釋衰還宮，百官辭於都城外。

translations.literal: The ancestor-offering was concluded; a halt was set outside the Gate of Bright Virtue; the farewell offering rite was performed; the mourning register was read; the emperor wept his fill; bowed twice in leave-taking; removed full mourning and returned to the palace; the hundred officials took leave outside the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: After the ancestor-offering was concluded, a halt was set outside the Gate of Bright Virtue for the farewell offering. The mourning register was read; the emperor wept his fill, bowed twice in farewell, removed full mourning and returned to the palace, while officials took their leave outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，掩皇堂。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day, the imperial chamber was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day the imperial burial chamber was sealed.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，虞主至，奉安於大明殿。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day the yu spirit tablet arrived and was respectfully installed in the Great Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the yu spirit tablet arrived and was installed in the Great Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 五月十九日，祔廟之第五室，以孝明皇后王氏升配。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the fifth month, enshrinement was made in the fifth chamber of the temple, with Empress Xiaoming née Wang elevated as consort.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the fifth month he was enshrined in the fifth chamber of the ancestral temple, with Empress Xiaoming née Wang elevated as his consort.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，群臣奉慰。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, the ministers offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the ministers offered condolences.

sentences.zh: 其吉凶仗如安陵，惟增轀輬車、神帛肩輿，鹵簿三千五百三十九人。

translations.literal: The auspicious and mourning processions were as at the An Mausoleum, only adding the enclosed hearse, spirit-silk shoulder litter, with an insignia guard of three thousand five hundred thirty-nine men.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious and mourning processions followed the An Mausoleum precedent, with only the addition of an enclosed hearse and a spirit-silk shoulder litter; the guard of honor numbered three thousand five hundred thirty-nine men.

sentences.zh: 陵在鞏縣，祔宣祖，曰永昌。

translations.literal: The mausoleum was in Gong County, enshrined with the Xuan Ancestor, and named Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb lay in Gong County, paired with the Xuan Ancestor, and was named Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 至道三年三月二十九日，太宗崩於萬歲殿。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month of the third year of Zhidao, Taizong died in the Hall of Myriad Years.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month in the third year of Zhidao, Taizong died in the Hall of Myriad Years.

sentences.zh: 真宗散發號擗，奉遺詔即位於殿之東楹。

translations.literal: Zhenzong loosened his hair and wailed, received the testamentary edict, and ascended the throne at the eastern pillar of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong let down his hair and wailed, then took the throne at the eastern pillar of the hall according to the final edict.

sentences.zh: 制永熙陵，皇堂深百尺，方廣八十尺，陵台方二百五十尺。

translations.literal: The Yongxi Mausoleum was established; the imperial chamber was one hundred feet deep, eighty feet square in area, and the tomb terrace two hundred fifty feet square.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongxi Mausoleum was planned with an imperial chamber one hundred feet deep and eighty feet square, and a tomb platform two hundred fifty feet on each side.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿，用玉輅一、革車五外，凡用九千四百六十八人。

translations.literal: For the great imperial insignia guard, one jade carriage and five leather carriages were used besides others; in all nine thousand four hundred sixty-eight men were employed.
translations.idiomatic: The grand imperial guard of honor employed one jade carriage and five leather carriages among others, with nine thousand four hundred sixty-eight men in all.

sentences.zh: 有司定散發之禮，皇帝、皇后、諸王、公主、縣主、諸王夫人、六宮內人並左被發，皇太后全被發。

translations.literal: The responsible offices fixed the rites for loosening the hair: the emperor, empress, imperial princes, princesses, commandery princesses, wives of imperial princes, and inner-palace women all had the left side of the hair loosened; the empress dowager had all the hair loosened.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices prescribed the rite of loosened hair: the emperor, empress, imperial princes, princesses, commandery princesses, wives of imperial princes, and inner-palace women all loosened the hair on the left side; the empress dowager loosened all her hair.

sentences.zh: 帝服布斜巾、四腳、大袖、裙、褲、帽，竹杖，腰絰、首絰，直領布衤蘭衫、白綾襯服。

translations.literal: The emperor wore hemp slanting band, four-cornered cap, large sleeves, skirt, trousers, and hat, bamboo staff, waist and head mourning cords, straight-collared hemp mourning shirt, and white silk under-robe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a hemp slanting band, four-cornered cap, wide sleeves, skirt, trousers, and hat, carried a bamboo staff, wore waist and head mourning cords, a straight-collared hemp mourning shirt, and a white silk under-robe.

sentences.zh: 諸王皇親以下如之，加布頭冠、絹礻親服。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, imperial kinsmen, and those below did likewise, adding hemp head cap and silk under-garment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, imperial kinsmen, and those below followed suit, adding hemp head caps and silk under-garments.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇后、內外命婦布裙、衫、帔、帕頭，首絰，絹礻親服。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, empress, and commissioned women inside and outside wore hemp skirts, shirts, shawls, and kerchiefs, head mourning cords, and silk under-garments.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, empress, and commissioned women inside and outside the palace wore hemp skirts, shirts, shawls, and kerchiefs, head mourning cords, and silk under-garments.

sentences.zh: 宮人無帔。

translations.literal: Palace women had no shawls.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women went without shawls.

sentences.zh: 文武二品以上布斜巾、四腳、頭冠、大袖、衤蘭衫、裙、褲，腰絰，竹杖，絹襯服。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the second rank and above wore hemp slanting bands, four-cornered caps, head caps, large sleeves, mourning shirts, skirts, trousers, waist mourning cords, bamboo staffs, and silk under-robes.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of the second rank and above wore hemp slanting bands, four-cornered caps, head caps, wide sleeves, mourning shirts, skirts, trousers, waist cords, bamboo staffs, and silk under-robes.

sentences.zh: 自餘百官並布襆頭、衤蘭衫，腰絰。

translations.literal: All remaining officials wore hemp wrapped headcloths, mourning shirts, and waist mourning cords.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials wore hemp wrapped headcloths, mourning shirts, and waist cords.

sentences.zh: 兩省五品、御史台尚書省四品、諸司三品以上，見任前任防禦、團練、刺史，內客省、閣門、入內都知、押班等，布頭冠、襆頭、大袖、衤蘭，衫、裙、褲，腰絰。

translations.literal: Fifth-rank officials of the two departments, fourth-rank officials of the Censorate and Secretariat-Chancellery, third-rank officials of the various bureaus and above, current and former defense commissioners, training commissioners, and prefects, Inner Service Bureau, Gatekeepers, Inner Palace Directors, duty officers, and the like wore hemp head caps, wrapped headcloths, large sleeves, mourning shirts, skirts, trousers, and waist mourning cords.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank officials of the two central departments, fourth-rank officials of the Censorate and Secretariat, third-rank officials of the various bureaus and above, current and former defense and training commissioners and prefects, Inner Service Bureau staff, gatekeepers, inner-palace directors, duty officers, and the like wore hemp head caps, wrapped headcloths, wide sleeves, mourning shirts, skirts, trousers, and waist cords.

sentences.zh: 諸軍、庶民白衫紙帽，婦人素縵不花釵，三日哭而止。

translations.literal: All armies and commoners wore white shirts and paper hats; women wore plain unpatterned dress without flowered hairpins; weeping ceased after three days.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and commoners wore white shirts and paper hats; women wore plain unpatterned dress without flowered hairpins; mourning cries ceased after three days.

sentences.zh: 山陵前，朔望不視事。

translations.literal: Before completion of the mausoleum, on new and full moon days he did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Until the tomb was finished, he did not conduct state business on new- and full-moon days.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔翰林寫先帝常服及絳紗袍、通天冠御容二，奉帳坐，列於大升輿之前，仍乙太宗玩好、弓劍、筆硯、琴棋之屬，蒙組繡置輿中，陳於仗內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict ordered the Hanlin to paint two portraits of the late emperor in regular dress and in crimson gauze robe with imperial cap, to be placed before the seat in the mourning canopy and arrayed before the great carrying litter; on the second day of the month Taizong's favorite objects—bows, swords, brush and inkstone, zither and chess set, and the like—wrapped in brocade, were placed in the litter and displayed within the procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict ordered the Hanlin Academy to paint two portraits of the late emperor in everyday dress and in crimson gauze robe with imperial cap, to be set before the seat in the mourning canopy and placed before the great carrying litter. On the following day Taizong's favorite objects—bows, swords, brush and inkstone, zither and chess set, and the like—wrapped in brocade, were placed in the litter and displayed within the funeral train.

sentences.zh: 十月三日，靈駕發引，其凶仗法物擎舁牽駕兵士力士，凡用萬二千一百九十三人。

translations.literal: On the third day of the tenth month the spirit carriage set out; for the mourning procession ritual objects, bearers, lifters, drivers, soldiers, and strongmen, twelve thousand one hundred ninety-three men were used in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the tenth month the spirit carriage departed. Bearers, lifters, drivers, soldiers, and strongmen for the mourning train's ritual objects numbered twelve thousand one hundred ninety-three men in all.

sentences.zh: 挽郎服白練寬衫、練裙，勒帛絹幘。

translations.literal: Mourning pullers wore white silk wide shirts, white silk skirts, and silk headcloths with belt bands.
translations.idiomatic: Pallbearers wore wide white silk shirts, white silk skirts, and silk headcloths with belt bands.

sentences.zh: 餘並如昌陵制。

translations.literal: The remainder all followed the regulations of the Chang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the Chang Mausoleum precedent.

sentences.zh: 十一月二日，有司奉神主至太廟，近臣題諡號，祔於第六室，以懿德皇后符氏升配。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eleventh month, the responsible offices presented the spirit tablet to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; close ministers inscribed the posthumous title; enshrinement was made in the sixth chamber, with Empress Yide née Fu elevated as consort.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eleventh month the responsible offices brought the spirit tablet to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; close ministers inscribed the posthumous title; he was enshrined in the sixth chamber, with Empress Yide née Fu elevated as his consort.

sentences.zh: 置衛十五百人於陵所，作殿以安御容，朝暮上食，四時致祭焉。

translations.literal: Fifteen hundred guards were stationed at the mausoleum site; a hall was built to install the imperial portrait; morning and evening food offerings were presented, and seasonal sacrifices were performed there.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen hundred guards were posted at the tomb; a hall was built to house the imperial portrait, with food offerings morning and evening and seasonal sacrifices throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，群臣入臨，見帝於東序。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day the ministers entered to attend; they saw the emperor in the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day the ministers came to attend; they found the emperor in the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 閣門使宣口敕曰：「先皇帝奄棄萬國，凡在臣僚，畢同號慕，及中外將校，並加存撫。」

translations.literal: The Gatekeeper Commissioner proclaimed an oral edict, stating: "The late emperor has suddenly abandoned the myriad realms; all who are subjects must together wail in grief, and both inner and outer military officers should likewise be shown care and reassurance."
translations.idiomatic: The Gatekeeper Commissioner proclaimed an oral edict: "The late emperor has suddenly left the realm; every subject must join in mourning, and military officers at court and in the provinces alike should be shown care and reassurance."

sentences.zh: 群臣拜舞稱萬歲，復哭盡哀，退。

translations.literal: The ministers bowed, danced, and hailed long life; then again wept their fill and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers bowed, performed the ritual dance, and hailed long life; then wept their fill again and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是日上表請聽政，凡三上，始允。

translations.literal: That day memorials requesting that he hear government were submitted; after three submissions permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That day memorials requesting that he resume governance were submitted three times before permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，陳先帝服玩及珠襦、玉匣、含、襚應入梓宮之物于延慶殿，召輔臣通觀。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day, the late emperor's garments and playthings, pearl shroud, jade casket, mouth-pearl, grave-gifts, and objects to enter the catalpa coffin were displayed in the Yanqing Hall; chief ministers were summoned to view them together.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day the late emperor's garments and personal objects, pearl shroud, jade casket, mouth-pearl, grave-gifts, and other items for the catalpa coffin were displayed in the Yanqing Hall, and chief ministers were summoned to inspect them together.

sentences.zh: 明日，大斂成服。

translations.literal: The next day, the great encoffining and assumption of mourning dress took place.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the great encoffining was performed and full mourning dress assumed.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，有司設御坐，垂簾崇政殿之西廡，簾幕皆縞素，群臣敘班殿門外。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day the responsible offices set the imperial seat and hung curtains in the western gallery of the Chongzheng Hall; all curtains were white hemp; the ministers formed ranks outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day the responsible offices set the imperial seat and hung curtains in the western gallery of the Chongzheng Hall, all in white hemp; the ministers formed ranks outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 帝衰服，去杖、絰，侍臣扶升坐。

translations.literal: The emperor in full mourning dress removed staff and mourning cords; attendants supported him as he ascended the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in full mourning, set aside staff and cords; attendants helped him to the seat.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引群臣入殿庭，西向合班。

translations.literal: The Communications Attendant led the ministers into the hall courtyard; they formed combined ranks facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Communications Attendant led the ministers into the hall courtyard, where they formed ranks facing west.

sentences.zh: 俟簾卷，群臣再拜，班首奏聖躬萬福，隨班三呼萬歲，退。

translations.literal: When the curtain was rolled up, the ministers bowed twice; the head of the rank reported the sacred person in myriad blessings; following the rank they thrice hailed long life, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the curtain was raised, the ministers bowed twice; the lead official reported that the sacred person was in good health; the assembly thrice hailed long life and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宰臣升殿奏事如儀。

translations.literal: The chief ministers ascended the hall and reported affairs according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers ascended the hall and reported affairs according to established ritual.

sentences.zh: 三月一日，小祥，帝行奠，釋衰服，群臣入臨，退，赴內東門，進名奉慰。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, at lesser mourning rites, the emperor performed the offering, removed full mourning dress; the ministers entered to attend; upon withdrawal they went to the inner eastern gate and submitted their names to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month, at lesser mourning, the emperor performed the offering and removed full mourning dress; the ministers came to attend, then went to the inner eastern gate to submit their names and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 自是每七日皆臨，至四十九日止。

translations.literal: From then on they attended every seven days until the forty-ninth day, when it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they attended every seven days until the forty-ninth day, when the practice ended.

sentences.zh: 十三日，大祥，帝釋服，服慘。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, at greater mourning rites, the emperor removed mourning dress and wore subdued dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day, at greater mourning, the emperor laid aside mourning dress and wore subdued dress.

sentences.zh: 十四日，司天監言：「山陵斬草，用四月一日丙時吉。」

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day the Directorate of Astronomy stated: "For cutting grass at the mausoleum, the third hour of the day on the first day of the fourth month is auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "For cutting the grass at the mausoleum site, the third hour of the day on the first day of the fourth month is auspicious."

sentences.zh: 十六日，山陵按行使藍繼宗言：「據司天監定永安縣東北六里曰臥龍岡，堪充山陵。」

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day, Lan Jizong, commissioner for inspecting the mausoleum site, stated: "According to the Directorate of Astronomy's designation, six li northeast of Yong'an County at a place called Crouching Dragon Mound is suitable to serve as the mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day Lan Jizong, commissioner for inspecting the mausoleum site, reported: "According to the Directorate of Astronomy, a site called Crouching Dragon Mound six li northeast of Yong'an County is suitable for the imperial tomb."

sentences.zh: 詔雷允恭覆按以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lei Yungong to re-inspect and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lei Yungong to reinspect the site and report back.

sentences.zh: 皇堂之制，深八十一尺，方百四十尺。

translations.literal: The regulations for the imperial chamber were eighty-one feet deep and one hundred forty feet square.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial burial chamber was designed to be eighty-one feet deep and one hundred forty feet square.

sentences.zh: 制陵名曰永定。

translations.literal: The mausoleum was established and named Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb was named Yongding.

sentences.zh: 九月十一日，召輔臣赴會慶殿，觀入皇堂物，皆生平服禦玩好之具。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the ninth month, chief ministers were summoned to the Huiqing Hall to view the objects for entering the imperial chamber, all being garments, imperial playthings, and favorite objects from his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the ninth month chief ministers were summoned to the Huiqing Hall to inspect the items for the burial chamber—everyday dress, personal objects, and favorite possessions from his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 帝與輔臣議及天書，皆先帝尊道膺受靈貺，殊尤之瑞屬於元聖，不可留於人間，宜於永定陵奉安。

translations.literal: The emperor and chief ministers discussed the Heavenly Writings, all being spiritual gifts received by the late emperor in reverence for the Way; these extraordinary auspicious signs belonged to the Primordial Sage and could not remain in the human realm—they should be respectfully installed at the Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and chief ministers discussed the Heavenly Writings, which the late emperor had received in reverence for the Way as divine gifts—extraordinary auspicious signs belonging to the Primordial Sage that could not remain in the human realm and should be installed at the Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，奉導天書至長春殿，帝上香再拜奉辭。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day the Heavenly Writings were respectfully escorted to the Changchun Hall; the emperor offered incense, bowed twice, and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day the Heavenly Writings were escorted to the Changchun Hall; the emperor offered incense, bowed twice, and bade them farewell.

sentences.zh: 二十四日，天書先發，帝啟奠梓宮，讀哀冊，禮畢，具吉凶儀仗。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day the Heavenly Writings departed first; the emperor performed the opening offering at the catalpa coffin, read the mourning register; when the rites were concluded, the auspicious and mourning insignia were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day the Heavenly Writings set out first; the emperor performed the opening offering at the catalpa coffin and read the mourning register; when the rites were finished, the auspicious and mourning processions were assembled.

sentences.zh: 百官素服赴順天門外，至板橋立班奉辭。

translations.literal: The hundred officials in plain dress went outside the Shuntian Gate, formed ranks at Banqiao, and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in plain dress went outside the Shuntian Gate, formed ranks at Banqiao, and bid the procession farewell.

sentences.zh: 還，詣西上閣門，進名奉慰。

translations.literal: Upon returning, they went to the western upper Gatehouse, submitted their names, and offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On returning they went to the western upper Gatehouse to submit their names and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 十月十三日，掩皇堂。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the tenth month, the imperial chamber was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the tenth month the imperial burial chamber was sealed.

sentences.zh: 十八日，虞主至京。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day the yu spirit tablet arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day the yu spirit tablet reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 十九日，群臣詣會慶殿行九虞祭。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the ministers went to the Huiqing Hall to perform the nine yu sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day the ministers went to the Huiqing Hall to perform the nine yu sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，祔太廟第七室。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day he was enshrined in the seventh chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day he was enshrined in the seventh chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年三月晦日，仁宗崩，英宗立。

translations.literal: On the last day of the third month of the eighth year of Jiayou, Renzong died and Yingzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the third month in the eighth year of Jiayou, Renzong died and Yingzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 喪服制度及修奉永昭陵，並用定陵故事，發諸路卒四萬六千七百人治之。

translations.literal: Mourning-garment regulations and the building and tending of the Yongzhao Mausoleum all followed the precedents of the Ding Mausoleum; soldiers from all circuits numbering forty-six thousand seven hundred men were dispatched to work on it.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress and construction of the Yongzhao Mausoleum followed the Ding Mausoleum precedent; forty-six thousand seven hundred soldiers from all circuits were mobilized for the work.

sentences.zh: 宣慶使石全彬提舉制梓宮，畫樣以進，命務堅完，毋過華飾。

translations.literal: Shi Quanbin, commissioner of the Xuanging Bureau, supervised manufacture of the catalpa coffin, submitted painted designs, and was ordered to ensure sturdiness and completeness without excessive ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Quanbin of the Xuanging Bureau supervised construction of the catalpa coffin, submitted designs for approval, and was instructed to make it solid and complete without excessive ornament.

sentences.zh: 三司請內藏錢百五十萬貫、槹絹二百五十萬匹、銀五十萬兩，助山陵及賞賚。

translations.literal: The Three Departments requested one million five hundred thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury, two million five hundred thousand bolts of silk and hemp, and five hundred thousand taels of silver to assist the mausoleum and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments requested one million five hundred thousand strings from the inner treasury, two million five hundred thousand bolts of silk and hemp, and five hundred thousand taels of silver for the tomb and rewards.

sentences.zh: 遣使告哀遼、夏及賜遺留物，又遣使告諭諸路。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to announce mourning to Liao and Xia and to bestow leftover objects; envoys were also sent to announce and instruct all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Liao and Xia and to present leftover personal effects; other envoys were dispatched to notify all circuits.

sentences.zh: 又以聽政奠告大行，近臣告升遐於天地、社稷、宗廟、宮觀，又告嗣位。

translations.literal: Offerings were also made upon hearing government to announce the Grand Journey; close ministers announced the ascension at Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, the ancestral temples, and palace shrines; the succession was also announced.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were made when governance resumed to announce the emperor's passing; close ministers announced his ascension at the altars of Heaven and Earth, soil and grain, ancestral temples, and palace shrines; the succession was announced as well.

sentences.zh: 賜兩府、宗室、近臣遺留物。

translations.literal: Leftover objects were bestowed on the two departments, the imperial clan, and close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Personal effects were distributed among the two central departments, the imperial clan, and close ministers.

sentences.zh: 五月，翰林學士王珪言：「天子之諡，當集中書門下御史台五品以上、尚書省四品以上、諸司三品以上，於南郊告天，議定，然後連奏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Hanlin Academician Wang Gui stated: "The Son of Heaven's posthumous title should gather officials of the fifth rank and above from the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate, fourth rank and above from the Secretariat, and third rank and above from the various bureaus, to announce to Heaven at the southern suburb, deliberate and fix it, and then submit jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Hanlin Academician Wang Gui argued: "The emperor's posthumous title should be determined by officials of the fifth rank and above from the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate, fourth rank and above from the Secretariat, and third rank and above from the various bureaus, who announce to Heaven at the southern suburb, deliberate, and then submit a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 近制唯詞臣撰議，即降詔命，庶僚不得參聞，頗違稱天之義。

translations.literal: Under recent regulations only literary officials draft the proposal and an edict is immediately issued; ordinary officials may not participate or hear, which considerably violates the meaning of addressing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent practice only literary officials draft the proposal and an edict follows immediately, excluding ordinary officials from participation—this considerably violates the principle of addressing Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣擬上先帝尊諡，望詔有司稽詳舊典，先之郊，而後下臣之議。」

translations.literal: Your subject proposes to present the late emperor's honored posthumous title; I hope an edict will order the responsible offices to examine the old regulations in detail, go first to the suburb, and afterward submit your subject's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: I propose to present the late emperor's posthumous title and ask that responsible offices be ordered to examine the old regulations, perform the suburban announcement first, and only then submit ministers' recommendations."

sentences.zh: 七月，宰臣以下宿尚書省，宗室團練使以上宿都亭驛，請諡於南郊。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, chief ministers and below lodged at the Secretariat; imperial clansmen of training commissioner rank and above lodged at the Duting Post Station, to request the posthumous title at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month chief ministers and below lodged at the Secretariat, while imperial clansmen of training commissioner rank and above stayed at the Duting Post Station to request the posthumous title at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 八月，告于福寧殿、天地、宗社、宮觀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, announcements were made at the Funing Hall, Heaven and Earth, the ancestral altars, and palace shrines.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month announcements were made at the Funing Hall, the altars of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and palace shrines.

sentences.zh: 九月二十八日，啟菆宮，以初喪服日一臨，易常服出。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month the encoffining palace was opened; once daily in initial mourning dress he attended, then changed to regular dress and went out.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month the encoffining hall was opened; the emperor attended once daily in initial mourning dress, then changed to regular dress before leaving.

sentences.zh: 十月六日，靈駕發引，天子啟奠，梓宮升龍輴。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the tenth month the spirit carriage set out; the Son of Heaven performed the opening offering; the catalpa coffin was raised onto the dragon hearse.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the tenth month the funeral procession departed; the emperor performed the opening offering and the catalpa coffin was lifted onto the dragon hearse.

sentences.zh: 祖奠徹，與皇太后步出宣德門，群臣辭於板橋。

translations.literal: The ancestor-offering was concluded; he walked out the Xuande Gate with the empress dowager; the ministers took leave at Banqiao.
translations.idiomatic: After the ancestor-offering was concluded, he walked out the Xuande Gate with the empress dowager while ministers bid farewell at Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 十五日，奉安梓宮陵側。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day the catalpa coffin was respectfully installed beside the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day the catalpa coffin was installed beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 十七日，開皇堂。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day the imperial chamber was opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day the imperial burial chamber was opened.

sentences.zh: 十一月二日，虞主至，皇太后奠于瓊林苑，天子步出集英殿門奉迎，奠於幄。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eleventh month the yu spirit tablet arrived; the empress dowager made offerings at the Qionglin Garden; the Son of Heaven walked out the Gate of the Hall of Assembled Excellence to welcome it and made offerings in the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eleventh month the yu spirit tablet arrived; the empress dowager made offerings at the Qionglin Garden; the emperor walked out the Gate of the Hall of Assembled Excellence to welcome it and made offerings in the mourning canopy.

sentences.zh: 七日，祭虞主。

translations.literal: On the seventh day the yu spirit tablet was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day sacrifices were offered to the yu spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，祔太廟。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 主如漢制，不題諡號，及終虞，而行卒哭之祭。

translations.literal: The tablet followed Han regulations, without inscribing the posthumous title; when the final yu rite was completed, the final weeping sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablet followed Han practice without inscribing the posthumous title; after the final yu rite the final weeping sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 禮院言：「故事，大祥變除服制，以三月二十九日大祥，至五月二十九日礻覃，六月二十九日禫除，至七月一日從吉，已蒙降敕。

translations.literal: The Ritual Academy stated: "According to precedent, the regulations for changing and removing dress at greater mourning rites set greater mourning on the twenty-ninth day of the third month, removal of the dan on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month, removal of mourning on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month, and return to auspicious dress on the first day of the seventh month; an edict has already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Academy reported: "According to precedent, dress changes at greater mourning set greater mourning on the twenty-ninth day of the third month, dan removal on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month, mourning removal on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month, and return to auspicious dress on the first day of the seventh month; an edict has already been issued.

sentences.zh: 謹按禮學，王肅以二十五月為畢喪，而鄭康成以二十七月，《通典》用其說，又加至二十七月終，則是二十八月畢喪，而二十九月始吉，蓋失之也。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining ritual learning, Wang Su held that mourning was completed in the twenty-fifth month, whereas Zheng Xuan held the twenty-seventh month; the Comprehensive Institutions adopted his view, and if one further extends to the end of the twenty-seventh month, then mourning is completed in the twenty-eighth month and auspicious dress begins in the twenty-ninth month—this is surely an error.
translations.idiomatic: Examining ritual scholarship, Wang Su held that mourning ended in the twenty-fifth month, while Zheng Xuan held the twenty-seventh; the Comprehensive Institutions followed Zheng's view, but if one extends to the end of the twenty-seventh month, mourning would end in the twenty-eighth and auspicious dress begin in the twenty-ninth—clearly an error.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，《更定五服年月敕》斷以二十七月，今士庶所同遵用。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, the Edict Revising the Years and Months of the Five Mourning Grades fixed it at the twenty-seventh month, which scholars and commoners alike now follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era the Edict Revising the Years and Months of the Five Mourning Grades fixed mourning at twenty-seven months, which scholars and commoners alike now follow.

sentences.zh: 夫三年之喪，自天子達，不宜有異。

translations.literal: The three-year mourning, extending from the Son of Heaven downward, should not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Three-year mourning extends from the Son of Heaven to the common people and should not differ.

sentences.zh: 請以三月二十九日為大祥，五月擇日而為禫，六月一日而從吉。」

translations.literal: We request that the twenty-ninth day of the third month be set as greater mourning, a day in the fifth month be chosen for the chan, and the first day of the sixth month for return to auspicious dress."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the twenty-ninth day of the third month be set as greater mourning, a day in the fifth month chosen for the chan rite, and the first day of the sixth month for return to auspicious dress."

sentences.zh: 於是大祥日不御前後殿，開封府停決大辟及禁屠至四月五日，待制、觀察使以上及宗室管軍官日一奠，二十八日而群臣俱入奠，二十九日禫除，群臣皆奉慰焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon on the day of greater mourning he did not attend the front and rear halls; Kaifeng Prefecture suspended capital sentences and banned slaughter until the fifth day of the fourth month; academicians, observation commissioners, and above, and imperial clansmen commanding armies made daily offerings; on the twenty-eighth day all ministers entered to make offerings; on the twenty-ninth day mourning was removed and all ministers offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, on greater mourning day he did not attend the front and rear halls; Kaifeng Prefecture suspended capital sentences and banned slaughter until the fifth day of the fourth month; academicians, observation commissioners, and above, and imperial clansmen commanding armies made daily offerings; on the twenty-eighth day all ministers came to offer sacrifices; on the twenty-ninth day mourning was removed and all ministers offered condolences.

sentences.zh: 治平四年正月八日，英宗崩，神宗即位。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the first month of the fourth year of Zhiping, Yingzong died and Shenzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the first month in the fourth year of Zhiping, Yingzong died and Shenzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一日，大斂。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day, the great encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day the great encoffining was performed.

sentences.zh: 二月三日，殯。

translations.literal: On the third day of the second month, the lying in state.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the second month the body was placed in the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 四月三日，請諡。

translations.literal: On the third day of the fourth month, the posthumous title was requested.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the fourth month the posthumous title was requested.

sentences.zh: 十八日，奏告及讀諡冊于福寧殿。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day, memorial announcement and reading of the posthumous-title register at the Funing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day the posthumous title was announced and the register read at the Funing Hall.

sentences.zh: 七月二十五日，啟菆。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month, the encoffining hall was opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month the encoffining hall was opened.

sentences.zh: 八月八日，靈駕發引。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eighth month the spirit carriage set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eighth month the funeral procession departed.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，葬永厚陵。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, burial at the Yonghou Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day he was buried at the Yonghou Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 禮院准禮：群臣成服後，乘布裹鞍韉。

translations.literal: The Ritual Academy approved according to ritual: after the ministers assumed mourning dress, they rode with hemp-wrapped saddles and saddlecloths.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Academy approved the ritual rule that after assuming mourning dress ministers rode horses with hemp-wrapped saddles and saddlecloths.

sentences.zh: 小祥臨訖，除頭冠、方裙、大袖。

translations.literal: When lesser mourning attendance was concluded, they removed head caps, square skirts, and large sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: When lesser mourning attendance ended, they removed head caps, square skirts, and wide sleeves.

sentences.zh: 大祥臨訖，裹素紗軟腳襆頭，慘公服，乘皂鞍韉。

translations.literal: When greater mourning attendance was concluded, they wore plain gauze soft-foot wrapped headcloths, subdued official dress, and rode with black saddles and saddlecloths.
translations.idiomatic: When greater mourning attendance ended, they wore plain gauze soft-foot wrapped headcloths and subdued official dress, and rode horses with black saddles and saddlecloths.

sentences.zh: 禫除訖，素紗襆頭、常服、黑帶。

translations.literal: When removal of mourning was concluded, plain gauze wrapped headcloths, regular dress, and black belts.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was removed they wore plain gauze wrapped headcloths, regular dress, and black belts.

sentences.zh: 二日，改吉服，去佩魚。

translations.literal: On the second day, they changed to auspicious dress and removed fish pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they changed to auspicious dress and removed fish pendants.

sentences.zh: 虞主至自掩壙，五虞皆在途，四虞于集英殿。

translations.literal: The yu spirit tablet arrived from the sealing of the tomb mound; five yu rites were all on the journey, four yu rites at the Hall of Assembled Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The yu spirit tablet arrived after the tomb was sealed; five yu rites were performed on the journey and four at the Hall of Assembled Excellence.

sentences.zh: 曲赦兩京、畿內、鄭、孟等州如故事。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted for the two capitals, the capital districts, Zheng, Meng, and other prefectures according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was granted for the two capitals, the capital districts, and prefectures such as Zheng and Meng, following precedent.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年三月五日，神宗崩。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the third month of the eighth year of Yuanfeng, Shenzong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the third month in the eighth year of Yuanfeng, Shenzong died.

sentences.zh: 十三日，大斂，帝成服。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, the great encoffining; the emperor assumed mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day the great encoffining was performed and the emperor assumed mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 十七日，小祥。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, lesser mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day lesser mourning was observed.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，禫除。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month mourning was removed.

sentences.zh: 七月五日，請諡於南郊。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the seventh month, the posthumous title was requested at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the seventh month the posthumous title was requested at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 九月八日，讀諡寶冊于福寧殿。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the ninth month, the posthumous-title register and seal were read at the Funing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the ninth month the posthumous register and seal were read at the Funing Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，啟菆。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day, the encoffining hall was opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day the encoffining hall was opened.

sentences.zh: 十月一日，靈駕發引。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, the spirit carriage set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month the funeral procession departed.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，葬永裕陵。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day, burial at the Yongyu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day he was buried at the Yongyu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二十九日，虞主至。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day the yu spirit tablet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day the yu spirit tablet arrived.

sentences.zh: 十一月一日，虞祭于集英殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, the yu sacrifice at the Hall of Assembled Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month the yu sacrifice was performed at the Hall of Assembled Excellence.

sentences.zh: 自復土，六虞在途，太常卿攝事，三虞行禮於殿。

translations.literal: From the returning of earth, six yu rites were on the journey; the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices acted in proxy; three yu rites were performed in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: From the time earth was returned to the tomb, six yu rites were performed on the journey with the Director of Imperial Sacrifices acting in proxy; three yu rites were performed in the hall.

sentences.zh: 四日，卒哭。

translations.literal: On the fourth day, the final weeping sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day the final weeping sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 五日，祔廟。

translations.literal: On the fifth day, enshrinement in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day he was enshrined in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 秘書正字范祖禹言：「先王制禮，以君服同于父，皆斬衰三年，蓋恐為人臣者不以父事其君，此所以管乎人情也。

translations.literal: Fan Zuyu, Corrector of Texts in the Secretariat, stated: "The former kings established ritual so that mourning for a lord was the same as for a father, all wearing the severest grade for three years—this was because they feared that subjects would not serve their lord as they serve a father; this is how human sentiment is governed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zuyu, Corrector of Texts in the Secretariat, argued: "The former kings established ritual so that mourning for a lord matched mourning for a father—three years in the severest grade—because they feared subjects would not serve their lord as they serve a father; this is how human sentiment is governed.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，不惟人臣無服，而人君遂亦不為三年之喪。

translations.literal: Since Han times, not only have subjects worn no mourning, but rulers themselves have also not observed three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times not only have subjects worn no mourning for their lord, but rulers themselves have not observed three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 唯國朝自祖宗以來，外廷雖用易月之制，而宮中實行三年之喪。

translations.literal: Only in our dynasty since the ancestors, although the outer court has used the system of substituting months, within the palace three-year mourning has actually been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Only in our dynasty, since the founding ancestors, has the outer court used the system of substituting months while the inner palace has actually practiced three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 且易月之制，前世所以難改者，以人君自不為服也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the system of substituting months was hard to change in previous ages was that the ruler himself did not wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reason previous dynasties found the month-substitution system hard to change was that the ruler himself did not wear mourning.

sentences.zh: 今群臣易月，而人主實行三年之喪，故十二日而小祥，期而又小祥，二十四日大祥，再期而又大祥。

translations.literal: Now the ministers substitute months while the ruler actually practices three-year mourning; thus lesser mourning on the twelfth day, lesser mourning again at one period, greater mourning on the twenty-fourth day, and greater mourning again at two periods.
translations.idiomatic: Today ministers substitute months while the ruler actually practices three-year mourning; hence lesser mourning on the twelfth day, lesser mourning again at one year, greater mourning on the twenty-fourth day, and greater mourning again at two years.

sentences.zh: 夫練、祥不可以有二也，既以日為之，又以月為之，此禮之無據者。

translations.literal: The lian and xiang rites cannot come in pairs; to perform them by days and also by months—this is ritual without basis.
translations.idiomatic: The lian and xiang rites cannot occur twice; to observe them by days and also by months is ritual without textual basis.

sentences.zh: 再期而大祥，中月而禫，禫者祭之名，非服之色也。

translations.literal: Greater mourning at two periods, chan in the middle month—chan is the name of a sacrifice, not the color of dress.
translations.idiomatic: Greater mourning at two years, chan in the middle month—chan is the name of a sacrifice, not a mourning color.

sentences.zh: 今乃為之慘服三日然後禫，此禮之不經者也。

translations.literal: Now subdued dress is worn for three days and only then chan is performed—this is ritual that has no classical warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Now subdued dress is worn for three days before chan is performed—this is ritual without classical warrant.

sentences.zh: 既除服，至葬而又服之，蓋不可以無服也。

translations.literal: Having removed mourning dress, at burial mourning is worn again—presumably because one cannot go without mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Having removed mourning dress, mourning is worn again at burial—presumably because one cannot go without mourning.

sentences.zh: 祔廟而後即吉，財八月矣，而遽純吉，無所不佩，此又禮之無漸也。

translations.literal: After enshrinement in the temple one immediately returns to auspicious dress—only eight months have passed, yet suddenly full auspicious dress with every ornament worn—this again is ritual without gradual transition.
translations.idiomatic: After enshrinement in the temple one immediately returns to full auspicious dress—only eight months have passed, yet suddenly every ornament is worn again—this is ritual without gradual transition.

sentences.zh: 易月之制，因襲已久，既不可追，宜令群臣朝服，止如今日而未除衰，至期而服之，漸除其重者，再期而又服之，乃釋衰，其餘則君服斯服可也。

translations.literal: The system of substituting months has been inherited for long and cannot now be reversed; ministers should be ordered to wear court dress, stopping as today without removing full mourning, wearing it at one period, gradually removing the heavier items, wearing it again at two periods, and only then releasing full mourning; for the rest, the ruler may wear whatever dress is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The month-substitution system has been inherited too long to reverse; ministers should wear court dress but, as today, not yet remove full mourning—wearing it at one year, gradually removing heavier items, wearing it again at two years, and only then releasing full mourning; for the rest, the ruler may wear whatever dress is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 至於禫，不必為之服，惟未純吉以至於祥，然後無所不佩，則三年之制略如古矣。」

translations.literal: As for chan, it is not necessary to wear dress for it; only when not yet fully auspicious until the xiang rite, and then wearing every ornament—then the three-year system would approximate the ancient."
translations.idiomatic: For chan it is unnecessary to wear special dress; only when not yet fully auspicious until the xiang rite, and then wearing every ornament, would the three-year system approximate antiquity."

sentences.zh: 詔禮官詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ritual officials to deliberate in detail.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書韓忠彥等議：「朝廷典禮，時世異宜，不必循古。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Han Zhongyan and others deliberated: "Court ceremonial codes differ in suitability from age to age and need not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Han Zhongyan and others argued: "Court ceremonial differs in suitability from age to age and need not follow antiquity.

sentences.zh: 若先王之制，不可盡用，則當以祖宗故事為法。

translations.literal: If the regulations of the former kings cannot all be used, then the precedents of the ancestors should be taken as law.
translations.idiomatic: If the former kings' regulations cannot all be applied, then ancestral precedents should serve as the standard.

sentences.zh: 今言者欲令群臣服喪三年，民間禁樂如之，雖過山陵，不去衰服，庶協古制。

translations.literal: The present proposal wishes to have ministers observe three-year mourning and the populace ban music likewise, and even after passing the mausoleum not remove full mourning dress, hoping thereby to accord with ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal would have ministers observe three-year mourning and the populace ban music likewise, and even after passing the mausoleum not remove full mourning dress, hoping to accord with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 緣先王恤典節文甚多，必欲循古，又非特如所言而已。

translations.literal: Because the condolence ceremonies of the former kings have very many detailed provisions, if one must follow antiquity, it is not only as the proposal states.
translations.idiomatic: Because the former kings' condolence ceremonies have many detailed provisions, following antiquity would require far more than the proposal states.

sentences.zh: 今既不能盡用，則當循祖宗故事及先帝遺制。」

translations.literal: Since they cannot all be used now, one should follow ancestral precedents and the late emperor's established regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Since they cannot all be applied now, one should follow ancestral precedents and the late emperor's established regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved their deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 神主祔廟，是月冬至，百官表賀。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple, that month at the winter solstice the hundred officials submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple, that month's winter solstice brought congratulatory memorials from all officials.

sentences.zh: 崇政殿說書程頤言：「神宗喪未除，節序變遷，時思方切，恐失居喪之禮，無以風化天下。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi, Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, stated: "Shenzong's mourning has not yet been removed; the seasons are changing; thoughts of the time are keen; I fear losing the ritual of dwelling in mourning and being unable to transform the realm by example.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, argued: "Shenzong's mourning has not yet ended; the seasons are changing and grief is still keen; I fear we will lose the ritual of dwelling in mourning and fail to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 乞改賀為慰。」

translations.literal: I beg that congratulations be changed to condolences."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that congratulations be changed to condolences."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，太史請遷去永裕陵禁山民塚一千三百餘，以便國音。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, the Grand Astrologer requested relocation of more than thirteen hundred commoners' tombs within the Yongyu Mausoleum restricted zone to facilitate the state's geomantic resonance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaosheng the Grand Astrologer requested relocation of more than thirteen hundred commoners' tombs within the Yongyu Mausoleum restricted zone to improve the site's geomantic resonance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遷墓得無擾乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Will relocating tombs not cause disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Will relocating tombs not cause disturbance?

sentences.zh: 若無所害，則令勿遷，果不便國音，當給官錢，以資葬費。」

translations.literal: If there is no harm, then order that they not be relocated; if it truly inconveniences the state's geomantic resonance, official money should be provided to cover burial expenses."
translations.idiomatic: If there is no harm, order that they not be moved; if relocation truly is needed for geomantic reasons, provide official funds to cover burial expenses."

sentences.zh: 元符三年正月十二日，哲宗崩，徽宗即位。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the first month of the third year of Yuanfu, Zhezong died and Huizong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the first month in the third year of Yuanfu, Zhezong died and Huizong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔山陵制度並如元豐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that mausoleum regulations all follow those of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that mausoleum regulations follow the Yuanfeng precedent.

sentences.zh: 七月十一日，啟菆。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the seventh month, the encoffining hall was opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the seventh month the encoffining hall was opened.

sentences.zh: 二十日，靈駕發引。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day, the spirit carriage set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day the funeral procession departed.

sentences.zh: 八月八日，葬永泰陵。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eighth month, burial at the Yongtai Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eighth month he was buried at the Yongtai Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 九月九日，以升祔畢，群臣吉服如故事。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month, because the elevation and enshrinement were completed, the ministers wore auspicious dress according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the ninth month, with the elevation and enshrinement completed, ministers wore auspicious dress according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 太常寺言：「太宗皇帝上繼太祖，兄弟相及，雖行易月之制，實斬衰三年，以重君臣之義。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "Emperor Taizong succeeded Taizu above him; brothers succeeded one another; although the system of substituting months was practiced, in fact the severest grade was worn for three years to emphasize the meaning of lord and subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Emperor Taizong succeeded Taizu; though brothers succeeded one another and the month-substitution system was used in public, he actually wore the severest mourning grade for three years to honor the bond between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 公除已後，庶事相稱，具載國史。

translations.literal: After public removal of mourning, all affairs were proportionate; this is fully recorded in the national history.
