translations.idiomatic: After public removal of mourning all state affairs were conducted appropriately, as fully recorded in the national history.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝嗣位哲宗，實承神考之世，已用開寶故事，為哲宗服衰重。

translations.literal: The present emperor succeeded Zhezong, in fact inheriting the era of the Divine Father; he has already used the Kaibao precedent and worn heavy full mourning for Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor succeeded Zhezong, inheriting the era of his divine father Shenzong, and has already followed the Kaibao precedent in wearing heavy full mourning for Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 今神主已祔，百官之服並用純吉，皇帝服禦宜如太平興國二年故事。」

translations.literal: Now that the spirit tablet has been enshrined, the dress of the hundred officials should all be fully auspicious; the emperor's dress should follow the precedent of the second year of Taiping Xingguo."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the spirit tablet has been enshrined, all officials should wear fully auspicious dress, and the emperor's attire should follow the precedent of the second year of Taiping Xingguo."

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「太平興國中，宰臣薛居正表稱：'公除以來，庶事相稱，獨命徹樂，誠未得宜。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites stated: "In Taiping Xingguo, Chief Minister Xue Juzheng memorialized, saying: 'Since public removal of mourning, all affairs have been proportionate; only the order to cease music is truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported: "During Taiping Xingguo, Chief Minister Xue Juzheng memorialized that since public removal of mourning all affairs had been proportionate, and that ordering music to cease was alone truly inappropriate.

sentences.zh: '即是公除後，除不舉樂外，釋衰從吉，事理甚明。

translations.literal: That is to say, after public removal, apart from not performing music, releasing full mourning and following auspicious dress—the principle is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: That is, after public removal of mourning, apart from not performing music, releasing full mourning and adopting auspicious dress—the principle is quite clear.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝當禦常服、素紗展腳襆頭、淡黃衫、黑犀帶，請下有司裁制。」

translations.literal: The present emperor should attend in regular dress, plain gauze extended-foot wrapped headcloth, pale yellow robe, and black rhinoceros-horn belt; we request that the responsible offices be ordered to prepare them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should now attend in regular dress, plain gauze extended-foot wrapped headcloth, pale yellow robe, and black rhinoceros-horn belt; we ask that responsible offices be ordered to prepare them.

sentences.zh: 宰臣請從禮官議，乃詔候週期服吉。

translations.literal: The chief ministers requested following the ritual officials' deliberation; an edict was then issued to await the completion of the mourning period before adopting auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked to follow the ritual officers' recommendation, and an edict was issued to await the completion of the mourning period before adopting auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 時詔不由門下，徑付有司。

translations.literal: At the time the edict did not pass through the Secretariat but was sent directly to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the edict bypassed the Secretariat and went directly to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 給事中龔原言：「喪制乃朝廷大事，今行不由門下，是廢法也。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Gong Yuan stated: "Mourning regulations are a great matter of the court; to carry them out now without passing through the Secretariat is to abolish the law.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gong Yuan argued: "Mourning regulations are a great matter of state; carrying them out without the Secretariat is to abolish the law.

sentences.zh: 臣為君服斬衰三年，古未嘗改。

translations.literal: Subjects wearing the severest grade for a lord for three years has never been changed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects wearing the severest mourning grade for their lord for three years has never been changed since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 且陛下前此議服，禮官持兩可之論，陛下既察見其奸，其服遂正。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty previously deliberated on mourning dress, the ritual officials held equivocal views; once Your Majesty perceived their deceit, the dress was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Your Majesty previously deliberated on mourning dress, ritual officials offered equivocal views; once Your Majesty perceived their deceit, mourning dress was corrected.

sentences.zh: 今乃不得已從之，臣竊為陛下惜。

translations.literal: Now you are compelled to follow them; your subject privately grieves for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now you are compelled to follow them, and I privately grieve for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 開寶時，並、汾未下，兵革未弭，祖宗櫛風沐雨之不暇，其服制權宜一時，非故事也。」

translations.literal: In Kaibao times Bing and Fen had not been taken, warfare was not stilled, and the ancestors had no leisure amid wind and rain; the mourning regulations were expedients for the moment, not precedents."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao times Bing and Fen had not been pacified and warfare had not ceased; the ancestors had no leisure amid hardship, and those mourning regulations were expedients for the moment, not established precedents.

sentences.zh: 原坐黜知南康軍。

translations.literal: Yuan was punished by demotion to prefect of Nankang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was demoted to prefect of Nankang Army for this offense.

sentences.zh: 於是詔依元降服喪三年之制，其元符三年九月「自小祥從吉」指揮，改正。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered following the originally issued regulation of three-year mourning; the directive of the ninth month of the third year of Yuanfu, "from lesser mourning follow auspicious dress," was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered adherence to the originally issued three-year mourning regulation, correcting the Yuanfu third-year ninth-month directive to adopt auspicious dress from lesser mourning.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年四月甲子，徽宗崩于五國城。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Shaoxing, Huizong died in the Five States City.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the fourth month in the fifth year of Shaoxing, Huizong died in the Five States City.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，問安使何蘚等還以聞，宰執入見，帝號慟擗踴，終日不食。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the envoys of inquiry He Xian and others returned to report; the chief ministers entered audience; the emperor wailed and beat his breast, and for a whole day ate nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year the inquiry envoys He Xian and others returned with the news; chief ministers came to audience; the emperor wailed and beat his breast and ate nothing all day.

sentences.zh: 宰臣張浚等力請，始進麋粥。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jun and others urgently pleaded, and only then was millet porridge brought.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jun and others urgently pleaded before he would take millet porridge.

sentences.zh: 成服于几筵殿，文武百僚朝晡臨於行宮。

translations.literal: Mourning dress was assumed at the Spirit Table Hall; civil and military officials of the hundred ranks attended morning and evening at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed mourning dress at the Spirit Table Hall; civil and military officials attended morning and evening at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 自聞喪至小祥，百官朝晡臨；

translations.literal: From hearing of the mourning until lesser mourning, the hundred officials attended morning and evening;
translations.idiomatic: From hearing of the mourning until lesser mourning, officials attended morning and evening;

sentences.zh: 自小祥至禫祭，朝一臨。

translations.literal: from lesser mourning until the chan sacrifice, they attended once each morning.
translations.idiomatic: from lesser mourning until the chan sacrifice, they attended once each morning.

sentences.zh: 太常等言：「舊制，沿邊州軍，不許舉哀。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and others stated: "Under old regulations, along the frontier prefectures and armies, mourning was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and others reported: "Under old regulations frontier prefectures and armies were not permitted to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 緣諸大帥皆國家腹心爪牙之臣，休戚一體，至於將佐，皆懷忠憤，宜就所屯，自副將而上成服，日朝晡臨，故校哭于本營。」

translations.literal: Because the great commanders are all the state's trusted inner and military servants, sharing fortune and misfortune as one body; as for their generals and aides, all harbor loyal indignation—they should at their encampments, from deputy commanders upward, assume mourning dress, attend morning and evening daily, and company officers weep in their own camps."
translations.idiomatic: Because the great commanders are the state's trusted military pillars who share its fortunes, and their generals and aides all harbor loyal indignation, they should at their encampments, from deputy commanders upward, assume mourning dress, attend morning and evening daily, and company officers weep in their own camps.

sentences.zh: 命徽猷閣待制王倫等為奉迎梓宮使。

translations.literal: Wang Lun, Attendant Drafting Master at the Huixian Pavilion, and others were appointed commissioners to welcome the catalpa coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun, Attendant Drafting Master at the Huixian Pavilion, and others were appointed commissioners to welcome the catalpa coffin.

sentences.zh: 時知邵州胡寅上疏，略曰：「三年之喪，自天子至於庶人，一也。

translations.literal: At the time Hu Yin, prefect of Shaozhou, submitted a memorial, stating in summary: "Three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven to the common people, is one.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu Yin, prefect of Shaozhou, submitted a memorial stating in summary: "Three-year mourning is the same for the Son of Heaven and the common people alike.

sentences.zh: 及漢孝文自執謙德，用日易月，至今行之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen of Han himself practiced modest virtue, he substituted days for months, and this has been practiced to the present.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen of Han practiced modest virtue he substituted days for months, and this has been practiced ever since.

sentences.zh: 子以便身忘其親，臣以便身忘其君，心知其非而不肯改，自常禮言之，猶且不可，況變故特異如今日者，又當如何？

translations.literal: Sons for their own convenience forget their parents; subjects for their own convenience forget their lords; knowing in their hearts it is wrong yet unwilling to change—even speaking from ordinary ritual, this is still not permissible; how much more when the change and calamity are as extraordinary as today?
translations.idiomatic: Sons forget their parents and subjects forget their lords for personal convenience, knowing it is wrong yet refusing to change—even by ordinary ritual this is unacceptable; how much more when the calamity is as extraordinary as today's?

sentences.zh: 恭惟大行太上皇帝、大行甯德皇后，蒙塵北狩，永訣不復，實由粘罕，是有不共戴天之仇。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the Grand Journey Supreme Emperor and the Grand Journey Mingde Empress, who suffered dust and were driven north on campaign, parted forever and cannot return—this was truly caused by Nianhan; there is a feud that cannot share heaven under one canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering the late Supreme Emperor and late Mingde Empress, who suffered disgrace and were driven north, never to return—this was truly caused by Nianhan; we bear a feud that cannot share heaven under one canopy.

sentences.zh: 考之于禮，仇不復則服不除，寢苫枕戈，無時而終。

translations.literal: Examining ritual, if the feud is not avenged mourning is not removed; sleeping on straw and using the spear as pillow, without end in time.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, if the feud is not avenged mourning is not removed; one should sleep on straw and use a spear as pillow without end.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，天下雖大，萬事雖眾，皆無以加于父子之恩，君臣之義也。

translations.literal: The reason is that though the realm is great and the myriad affairs numerous, nothing can be placed above the grace between father and son and the righteousness between lord and subject.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that though the realm is vast and affairs innumerable, nothing surpasses the bond between father and son or the duty between lord and subject.

sentences.zh: 伏睹某月某日聖旨，緣國朝故典，以日易月，臣切以為非矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen the sacred directive of such-and-such month and day, citing the dynasty's old regulations to substitute days for months; your subject firmly believes this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the imperial directive of such-and-such date citing the dynasty's old regulations to substitute days for months, and I firmly believe this is wrong.

sentences.zh: 自常禮言之，猶須大行有遺詔，然後遵承。

translations.literal: Speaking from ordinary ritual, there must still be a testamentary edict from the Grand Journey before compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Even by ordinary ritual there must be a testamentary edict from the late emperor before such a practice may be followed.

sentences.zh: 今也大行詔旨不聞，而陛下降旨行之，是以日易月，出陛下意也。

translations.literal: Now no edict from the Grand Journey has been heard, yet Your Majesty has issued a directive to carry it out—thus substituting days for months comes from Your Majesty's own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now no edict from the late emperor has been heard, yet Your Majesty has issued a directive to carry it out—substituting days for months thus comes from Your Majesty's own intent.

sentences.zh: 大行幽厄之中，服禦飲食，人所不堪，疾病粥藥，必無供億，崩殂之後，衣衾斂藏，豈得周備？

translations.literal: The Grand Journey in dire confinement—dress, carriage, food and drink that humans cannot endure; illness, gruel and medicine surely without provision; after death, shrouds and encoffining—how could they be complete?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor in dire confinement endured dress, food, and drink beyond human endurance; in illness there was surely no provision of gruel and medicine; after death, were shrouds and encoffining complete?

sentences.zh: 正棺卜兆，知在何所？

translations.literal: Proper coffining and divination of the site—who knows where they are?
translations.idiomatic: Proper coffining and choice of burial site—who knows where they are?

sentences.zh: 茫茫沙漠，瞻守為誰？

translations.literal: In the vast desert, for whom shall we gaze and guard?
translations.idiomatic: In the vast desert, for whom shall we gaze and keep watch?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下一念及此，荼毒摧割，備難堪忍，縱未能遵《春秋》復仇之義，俟仇殄而後除服，猶當革漢景之薄，喪紀以三年為斷。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that if Your Majesty reflects on this once, the anguish is crushing and hard to bear; even if unable to follow the Spring and Autumn Annals' principle of avenging a feud and removing mourning only after the enemy is destroyed, one should still reform the thinness of Emperor Jing of Han and fix mourning at three years.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reflects on this once, the anguish is crushing beyond endurance; even if unable to follow the Spring and Autumn Annals and remove mourning only after the enemy is destroyed, one should still reform Emperor Jing of Han's thin practice and fix mourning at three years.

sentences.zh: 不然，以終身不可除之服，二十七日而除之，是薄之中又加薄焉，必非聖人之所安也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, to take mourning that should never be removed in a lifetime and remove it in twenty-seven days is to add thinness upon thinness; this surely cannot be what the sage would find acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, to remove in twenty-seven days mourning that should never be removed in a lifetime is to add thinness upon thinness; this surely cannot be what a sage would find acceptable."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雖宅憂三祀，而軍旅之事，皆當決於聖裁，則諒沍之典，有不可舉。

translations.literal: He further said: "Although dwelling in mourning for three years, military affairs should all be decided by sacred judgment; thus the rites of sincere mourning cannot all be performed.
translations.idiomatic: He further said: "Although dwelling in mourning for three years, military affairs must still be decided by imperial judgment, so the full rites of sincere mourning cannot all be performed.

sentences.zh: 蓋非枕塊無聞之日，是乃枕戈有事之辰，故魯侯有周公之喪，而徐夷並興，東郊不開，則是墨衰即戎，孔子取其誓命。

translations.literal: For this is not the time of resting on clods in silence, but the time of resting on spears with affairs pending; thus when the Lord of Lu had the Duke of Zhou's mourning and the Xu and Yi both rose, the eastern suburb did not open—then wearing ink mourning and taking up arms, Confucius approved his sworn command.
translations.idiomatic: For this is not a time to rest on clods in silence but a time to rest on spears with affairs pending; when the Lord of Lu mourned the Duke of Zhou and the Xu and Yi both rose, the eastern suburb did not open—he wore ink mourning and took up arms, which Confucius approved in his sworn command.

sentences.zh: 今六師戒嚴，方將北討，萬幾之眾，孰非軍務。

translations.literal: Now the six armies are on alert; a northern campaign is about to be launched; of the myriad affairs, which is not military business?
translations.idiomatic: Now the six armies are on alert and a northern campaign is imminent; of the myriad state affairs, which is not military business?

sentences.zh: 陛下聽斷平決，得禮之變，卒哭之後，以墨衰臨朝，合於孔子所取，其可行無疑也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty hearing and deciding cases in judgment obtains the ritual variation; after the final weeping sacrifice, attending court in ink mourning accords with what Confucius approved—it can be carried out without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's hearing and deciding cases embodies the ritual variation; after the final weeping sacrifice, attending court in ink mourning accords with what Confucius approved and may be carried out without doubt.

sentences.zh: 如合聖意，便乞直降詔旨雲'恭惟太上皇帝、甯德皇后，誕育眇躬，大恩難報，欲酬罔極，百未一伸。

translations.literal: If this accords with sacred intent, your subject begs that an edict be directly issued, saying: 'Respectfully considering the Supreme Emperor and the Mingde Empress, who gave birth to my humble person—great grace hard to repay, wishing to repay without limit, not one part in a hundred fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: If this accords with Your Majesty's intent, I beg that an edict be directly issued, saying: 'Respectfully considering the Supreme Emperor and Mingde Empress, who gave birth to my humble person—great grace hard to repay, wishing to repay without limit, not one part in a hundred fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 鑾輿遠征，遂至大故，訃音所至，痛貫五情。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went on distant campaign and thus came to great calamity; where the news of death arrived, pain pierced the five emotions.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage went on distant campaign and met great calamity; where the news of death arrived, pain pierced my whole being.

sentences.zh: 想慕慈顏，杳不復見，怨仇有在，朕敢忘之。

translations.literal: Longing for the kindly countenance, it is lost and cannot be seen again; the feud enemy exists—how dare I forget?
translations.idiomatic: Longing for that kindly face, lost never to be seen again; the feud enemy still lives—how dare I forget?

sentences.zh: 雖軍國多虞，難以諒闇，然衰麻枕戈，非異人任。

translations.literal: Although the army and state have many concerns and sincere mourning is hard to practice, yet wearing hemp mourning and resting on spears is no task for another.
translations.idiomatic: Although army and state have many concerns and sincere mourning is hard to practice, wearing hemp mourning while resting on spears is no task for another to perform.

sentences.zh: 以日易月，情所不安，興自朕躬，致喪三年。

translations.literal: Substituting days for months is what the feelings cannot accept; arising from my own person, I institute three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Substituting days for months is what my feelings cannot accept; arising from my own person, I institute three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 即戎衣墨，況有權制，佈告中外，昭示至懷。

translations.literal: Taking up arms in ink dress, moreover with expedient regulations, proclaim to inner and outer, displaying utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Taking up arms in ink mourning dress, with expedient regulations besides, proclaim this within and without to display my utmost feeling.

sentences.zh: 其合行典禮，令有司集議來上。

translations.literal: As for the ceremonial codes to be carried out, order the responsible offices to assemble deliberations and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the ceremonial codes to be carried out, order responsible offices to assemble deliberations and submit them.

sentences.zh: 如敢沮格，是使朕為人子而忘孝之道，當以大不恭論其罪。

translations.literal: If anyone dares obstruct it, this would make me as a son forget the way of filial piety; obstruction should be judged as great irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone dares obstruct it, this would make me as a son forget filial duty; obstruction should be judged as great irreverence.

sentences.zh: '陛下親禦翰墨，自中降出，一新四方耳目，以化天下，天地神明，亦必有以佑助。

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty personally wield the brush, issuing it from within, renewing the ears and eyes of the four quarters, to transform the realm—Heaven, Earth, and the spirits will surely lend aid.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty personally wield the brush and issue it from within, renewing the ears and eyes of the realm to transform the world—Heaven, Earth, and the spirits will surely lend aid.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝大願。」

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear his great wish."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot express his great hope sufficiently."

sentences.zh: 徽宗與顯肅初葬五國城，十二年，金人以梓宮來還。

translations.literal: Huizong and Xiansu were first buried in the Five States City; in the twelfth year the Jin people returned the catalpa coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong and Empress Xiansu were first buried in the Five States City; in the twelfth year the Jin returned the catalpa coffin.

sentences.zh: 將至，帝服黃袍乘輦，詣臨平奉迎，登舟易緦服，百官皆如之。

translations.literal: As it was about to arrive, the emperor in yellow robe rode the palanquin, went to Linping to welcome it, boarded the boat and changed to finest mourning, and the hundred officials all did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: As it was about to arrive, the emperor in yellow robe rode the palanquin to Linping to welcome it, then boarded the boat and changed to finest mourning, as did all officials.

sentences.zh: 既至行在，安奉于龍德別宮，帝后異殿。

translations.literal: Once it reached the traveling capital, it was respectfully installed in the Longde Separate Palace, emperor and empress in separate halls.
translations.idiomatic: Once it reached the traveling capital, it was installed in the Longde Separate Palace, with separate halls for emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 禮官請用安陵故事，梓宮入境，即承之以槨；

translations.literal: The ritual officials requested using the An Mausoleum precedent: when the catalpa coffin entered the border, it was immediately received with an outer coffin;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials requested the An Mausoleum precedent: when the catalpa coffin entered the border it was immediately placed in an outer coffin;

sentences.zh: 有司預備袞冕、翬衣以往，至則納之槨中，不復改斂。

translations.literal: the responsible offices prepared the nine-symbol robe and crown and pheasant robes to take there; upon arrival they were placed in the outer coffin without re-encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: responsible offices prepared imperial robes and pheasant-embroidered dress to take there; upon arrival they were placed in the outer coffin without re-encoffining.

sentences.zh: 秦檜白令侍從、台諫、禮官集議，靈駕既還，當崇奉陵寢，或稱欑宮。

translations.literal: Qin Hui reported ordering attendant officials, remonstrance officials, and ritual officials to assemble deliberations: since the spirit carriage had returned, the mausoleum chamber should be honored and tended, or it might be called the encoffining palace.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui ordered attendant officials, remonstrance officials, and ritual officials to deliberate: since the spirit carriage had returned, the tomb should be honored and tended, or called the encoffining palace.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎程敦厚希檜意，獨上奏言：「仍欑宮之舊稱，則莫能示通和之大信，而用因山之正典，則若亡存本之後圖。

translations.literal: Cheng Dunhou, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, hoping to please Qin Hui, alone submitted a memorial stating: "To retain the old title of encoffining palace cannot display the great trust of reconciliation; yet to use the proper canon of burial on the mountain seems like forgetting survival and preserving the foundation for later plans.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dunhou, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, hoping to please Qin Hui, alone memorialized: "Retaining the old title of encoffining palace cannot display the great trust of reconciliation, yet using the proper canon of mountain burial seems like abandoning survival for later plans.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜勿褟虛名，當示大信。」

translations.literal: Your subject believes one should not dress up empty names but should display great trust."
translations.idiomatic: I believe one should not dress up empty names but should display great trust.

sentences.zh: 於是議者工部尚書莫將等乃言：「太史稱歲中不利大葬，請用明德皇后故事，權欑。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the deliberators, Minister of Works Mo Jiang and others, stated: "The Grand Astrologer said the year was unfavorable for great burial; we request using the precedent of Empress Mingde and provisionally encoffining."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Mo Jiang, Minister of Works, and other deliberators stated: "The Grand Astrologer said the year was unfavorable for great burial; we request using Empress Mingde's precedent and provisionally encoffining.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 以八月奉迎，九月發引，十月掩欑，在昭慈欑宮西北五十步，用地二百五十畝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month it was welcomed; in the ninth month the procession set out; in the tenth month the encoffining was sealed, fifty paces northwest of the Zhaoci Encoffining Palace, using two hundred fifty mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: It was welcomed in the eighth month, the procession set out in the ninth, and encoffining was sealed in the tenth, fifty paces northwest of the Zhaoci Encoffining Palace on two hundred fifty mu of land.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改陵名曰永祐。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the mausoleum name was changed to Yongyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the tomb was renamed Yongyou.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年五月，金國使至，以欽宗訃聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirty-first year of Shaoxing, a Jin envoy arrived announcing Qinzong's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirty-first year of Shaoxing a Jin envoy arrived announcing Qinzong's death.

sentences.zh: 詔：「朕當持斬衰三年之服，以申哀慕。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "I shall wear the severest grade for three years to express grief and longing."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "I shall wear the severest mourning grade for three years to express grief and longing.

sentences.zh: 是日，文武百僚並常服、黑帶，去魚，詣天章閣南空地立班，聽詔旨，舉哭畢，次赴後殿門外進名奉慰，次詣几筵殿焚香舉哭。

translations.literal: That day, civil and military officials of the hundred ranks all in regular dress and black belts, fish pendants removed, went to the open ground south of the Tianzhang Pavilion, formed ranks, heard the edict, concluded the mourning cries, next went outside the rear hall gate to submit names and offer condolences, next went to the Spirit Table Hall to burn incense and mourn.
translations.idiomatic: That day civil and military officials in regular dress and black belts, fish pendants removed, formed ranks on the open ground south of the Tianzhang Pavilion, heard the edict and concluded mourning cries, then went outside the rear hall gate to submit names and offer condolences, then to the Spirit Table Hall to burn incense and mourn.

sentences.zh: 六月，權禮部侍郎金安節等請依典故，以日易月，自五月二十二日立重，安奉几筵，至六月十七日大祥，所有衰服，權留以待梓宮之還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Acting Vice Minister of Rites Jin Anjie and others requested following precedent to substitute days for months; from the twenty-second day of the fifth month the spirit seat was established and the spirit table installed; until the seventeenth day of the sixth month for greater mourning—all full mourning dress was provisionally retained awaiting return of the catalpa coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Acting Vice Minister of Rites Jin Anjie and others requested following precedent to substitute days for months; from the twenty-second day of the fifth month the spirit seat was established until the seventeenth day of the sixth month for greater mourning—all full mourning dress was provisionally retained awaiting return of the catalpa coffin.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 七月，宰臣陳康伯等率百官詣南郊請諡，廟號欽宗，遙上陵名曰永獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Chief Minister Chen Kangbo and others led the hundred officials to the southern suburb to request the posthumous title; temple name Qinzong; the distant mausoleum name was presented as Yongxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chief Minister Chen Kangbo and others led officials to the southern suburb to request the posthumous title; temple name Qinzong; the distant tomb was named Yongxian.

sentences.zh: 其餘並如徽宗典禮。

translations.literal: The remainder all followed Huizong's ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed Huizong's ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年十月八日，高宗崩，孝宗號慟擗踴，逾二日不進膳。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Chunxi, Gaozong died; Xiaozong wailed and beat his breast, and for more than two days took no meal.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the tenth month in the fourteenth year of Chunxi, Gaozong died; Xiaozong wailed and beat his breast and for more than two days took no food.

sentences.zh: 尋諭宰執王淮，欲不用易月之制，如晉武、魏孝文實行三年之喪，自不妨聽政。

translations.literal: Soon he instructed Chief Minister Wang Huai that he wished not to use the system of substituting months, but like Emperor Wu of Jin and Emperor Xiaowen of Wei actually practice three-year mourning, which would not hinder hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he told Chief Minister Wang Huai that he wished not to use month substitution but, like Emperor Wu of Jin and Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, actually practice three-year mourning, which would not hinder governance.

sentences.zh: 淮等奏：「《通鑒》載晉武帝雖有此意，後來只是宮中深衣、練冠。」

translations.literal: Huai and others memorialized: "The Comprehensive Mirror records that although Emperor Wu of Jin had this intent, afterward it was only deep robes and lian caps within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Huai and others memorialized: "The Comprehensive Mirror records that although Emperor Wu of Jin had this intent, afterward it was only deep robes and lian caps within the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「當時群臣不能將順其美，司馬光所以譏之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At the time the ministers could not follow and harmonize with his excellence; this is why Sima Guang ridiculed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "At the time the ministers could not follow and support his intent; that is why Sima Guang ridiculed them.

sentences.zh: 後來武帝竟欲行之。」

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wu ultimately wished to carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu ultimately wished to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「記得亦不能行。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "As I recall, he could not carry it out either."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said: "As I recall, he could not carry it out either.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「自我作古何害？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What harm is there in my making the ancient anew?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What harm is there in my making the ancient anew?

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「禦殿之時，人主衰絰，群臣吉服，可乎？」

translations.literal: Huai said: "When attending the imperial hall, the ruler in full mourning cords and ministers in auspicious dress—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai said: "When attending the imperial hall, the ruler in full mourning cords and ministers in auspicious dress—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「自有等降。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There are naturally grades and distinctions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "There are naturally grades and distinctions.

sentences.zh: 乃出內批：「朕當衰絰三年，群臣自行易月之令。

translations.literal: An inner endorsement was then issued: "I shall wear full mourning cords for three years; the ministers shall themselves follow the order of substituting months.
translations.idiomatic: An inner endorsement was then issued: "I shall wear full mourning cords for three years; ministers shall themselves follow the order of substituting months.

sentences.zh: 其合行儀制，令有司討論。」

translations.literal: As for the ritual regulations to be carried out, order the responsible offices to discuss them."
translations.idiomatic: As for the ritual regulations to be carried out, order responsible offices to discuss them.

sentences.zh: 詔百官于以日易月之內，衰服治事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials that within the period of substituting days for months they should conduct affairs in full mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that within the period of substituting days for months officials should conduct affairs in full mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 二十日丁亥，小祥，帝未改服，王淮等乞俯從禮制。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day, the twentieth, at lesser mourning the emperor had not changed dress; Wang Huai and others begged him to comply with ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day, the twentieth, at lesser mourning the emperor had not changed dress; Wang Huai and others begged him to comply with ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 上流涕曰：「大恩難報，情所未忍。」

translations.literal: The emperor, weeping, said: "Great grace is hard to repay; my feelings cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, weeping, said: "Great grace is hard to repay; my feelings cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，車駕還內，帝衰絰禦輦，設素仗，軍民見者，往往感泣。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day the imperial carriage returned within; the emperor in full mourning cords attended the palanquin; plain insignia were set out; soldiers and civilians who saw it often wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day the imperial carriage returned within; the emperor in full mourning cords rode the palanquin with plain insignia; soldiers and civilians who saw it often wept.

sentences.zh: 詔自今五日一詣梓宮前焚香。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on every five days he should go before the catalpa coffin to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that from now on every five days he should go before the catalpa coffin to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 帝欲衰服素幄，引輔臣及班次，而禮官奏謂：「苴麻三年，難行於外庭。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to wear full mourning in a plain canopy and summon chief ministers and ranks, but the ritual officials memorialized: "Raw hemp for three years is hard to practice in the outer court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to wear full mourning in a plain canopy and summon chief ministers and ranks, but ritual officials memorialized: "Raw hemp mourning for three years is hard to practice in the outer court.

sentences.zh: 奏入，不出。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; no response was issued.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊戍朔，禮官顏師魯、尤袤等奏：「乞禮畢改服小祥之服，去杖、絰。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, the wuxu day, ritual officials Yan Shilu, You Mao, and others memorialized: "We beg that when the rites are concluded dress be changed to lesser mourning dress, removing staff and cords.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month ritual officials Yan Shilu, You Mao, and others memorialized: "We beg that when the rites are concluded dress be changed to lesser mourning dress, removing staff and cords.

sentences.zh: 禫祭禮畢，改服素紗軟腳折上巾、淡黃袍、黑銀帶。

translations.literal: When the chan sacrifice rites were concluded, change to plain gauze soft-foot folded-up cap, pale yellow robe, and black silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: When the chan sacrifice rites were concluded, change to plain gauze soft-foot folded cap, pale yellow robe, and black silver belt.

sentences.zh: 神主祔廟畢，改服皂襆頭、黑鞓犀帶。

translations.literal: When enshrinement of the spirit tablet in the temple was concluded, change to black wrapped headcloth and black rhinoceros-horn belt with dark purple fittings.
translations.idiomatic: When enshrinement of the spirit tablet was concluded, change to black wrapped headcloth and black rhinoceros-horn belt with dark purple fittings.

sentences.zh: 遇過宮燒香，則于宮中衰絰行禮，二十五月而除。」

translations.literal: When passing the palace to burn incense, then perform rites in full mourning cords within the palace; removed in the twenty-fifth month."
translations.idiomatic: When passing the palace to burn incense, perform rites in full mourning cords within the palace; mourning removed in the twenty-fifth month.

sentences.zh: 帝批：「淡黃袍改服白袍。」

translations.literal: The emperor endorsed: "Change the pale yellow robe to a white robe."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed: "Change the pale yellow robe to a white robe.

sentences.zh: 二日己亥，大祥。

translations.literal: On the jihai day, the second, greater mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day, the second, greater mourning.

sentences.zh: 四日辛丑，禫祭禮畢。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day, the fourth, the chan sacrifice rites were concluded.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, the fourth, the chan sacrifice rites were concluded.

sentences.zh: 五日壬寅，百官請聽政，不允。

translations.literal: On the renyin day, the fifth, the hundred officials requested that he hear government; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, the fifth, officials requested that he resume governance; permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 八日，百官三上表，引《康誥》「被冕服出應門」等語以證。

translations.literal: On the eighth day the hundred officials submitted memorials three times, citing the Announcement to Kang phrases such as "wearing the cap and robe, going out the Ying Gate" as proof.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day officials submitted memorials three times, citing the Announcement to Kang phrases such as "wearing cap and robe, going out the Ying Gate" as proof.

sentences.zh: 九日，詔可。

translations.literal: On the ninth day, an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月十八日甲寅，百日，帝過宮行焚香禮。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, the eighteenth of the first month of the fifteenth year, the hundredth day, the emperor passed the palace to perform the incense-burning rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day, the eighteenth of the first month in the fifteenth year, the hundredth day, the emperor went to the palace to perform the incense-burning rite.

sentences.zh: 二十一日丁巳，諭輔臣曰：「昨內引洪邁，見朕已過百日，猶服衰粗因奏事應以漸，今宜服如古人墨衰之義，而巾則用繒或羅。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day, the twenty-first, he instructed the chief ministers: "Yesterday I summoned Hong Mai within; he saw that I had passed the hundredth day yet still wore coarse full mourning when reporting affairs, which should gradually change; now I should dress according to the ancient meaning of ink mourning, but the headcloth should use silk gauze or gauze.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, the twenty-first, he told the chief ministers: "Yesterday I summoned Hong Mai within; he saw that I had passed the hundredth day yet still wore coarse full mourning when reporting affairs, which should gradually change; now I should dress according to the ancient meaning of ink mourning, but the headcloth should use silk gauze or gauze.

sentences.zh: 朕以羅絹非是，若用細布則可。」

translations.literal: I consider silk gauze and silk unsuitable; if fine cloth is used, that will do."
translations.idiomatic: I consider silk gauze and silk unsuitable; fine cloth would be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 王淮等言：「尋常士大夫丁憂過百日，巾衫皆用細布，出而見客，則以黲布。

translations.literal: Wang Huai and others said: "Ordinarily when scholar-officials observe mourning for a parent past the hundredth day, headcloths and shirts all use fine cloth; when going out to receive guests, they use gray cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai and others said: "Ordinarily when scholar-officials observe mourning for a parent past the hundredth day, headcloths and shirts use fine cloth; when going out to receive guests, they use gray cloth.

sentences.zh: 今陛下舉曠古不能行之禮，足為萬世法。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is practicing ritual that antiquity could not carry out—sufficient to serve as law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is practicing ritual that antiquity could not carry out—sufficient to serve as a model for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 帝又曰：「晚間引宿直官之類如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor further said: "How about summoning night-duty officials and the like in the evening?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further said: "How about summoning night-duty officials and the like in the evening?

sentences.zh: 淮曰：「布巾、布背子便是常服。」

translations.literal: Huai said: "Cloth headcloth and cloth jacket are regular dress."
translations.idiomatic: Huai said: "Cloth headcloth and cloth jacket are regular dress.

sentences.zh: 上不以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consider this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 自是每禦延和殿，止服白布折上巾、布衫，過宮則衰絰而杖。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he attended the Yanhe Hall, he wore only white cloth folded-up cap and cloth shirt; when passing the palace he wore full mourning cords and carried a staff.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever he attended the Yanhe Hall, he wore only a white cloth folded cap and cloth shirt; when going to the palace he wore full mourning cords and carried a staff.

sentences.zh: 三月壬子，啟欑，帝服初喪之服。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the third month, the encoffining hall was opened; the emperor wore initial mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the third month the encoffining hall was opened; the emperor wore initial mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，發引。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, the procession set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day the funeral procession departed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，掩欑。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day, the encoffining was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day the encoffining was sealed.

sentences.zh: 甲戍，親行第七虞祭。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, he personally performed the seventh yu sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he personally performed the seventh yu sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大臣言：「虞祭乃吉禮，合用靴袍。」

translations.literal: The great ministers stated: "The yu sacrifice is an auspicious rite and should use boots and robe."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers stated: "The yu sacrifice is an auspicious rite and should use boots and formal robe.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「只用布折上巾、黑帶、布袍可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Only cloth folded-up cap, black belt, and cloth robe will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A cloth folded cap, black belt, and cloth robe will suffice."

sentences.zh: 二十日丙戍，神主祔廟。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day, the twentieth, the spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day, the twentieth, the spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple.

sentences.zh: 是日詔曰：「朕昨降指揮，欲衰絰三年，緣群臣屢請禦殿易服，故以布素視事內殿。

translations.literal: That day an edict stated: "I yesterday issued a directive wishing to wear full mourning cords for three years; because the ministers repeatedly requested changing dress to attend the hall, I therefore conducted affairs in the inner hall in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict stated: "I yesterday issued a directive wishing to wear full mourning cords for three years; because ministers repeatedly requested that I change dress to attend the hall, I conducted affairs in the inner hall in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 雖有俟過祔廟勉從所請之詔，稽諸典禮，心實未安，行之終制。

translations.literal: Although there was an edict to wait until after enshrinement in the temple and reluctantly follow the request, examining the ceremonial codes, my heart was truly not at ease; I shall carry out the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Although there was an edict to wait until after enshrinement and reluctantly follow the request, examining the ceremonial codes, my heart was truly uneasy; I shall carry out the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 乃為近古。

translations.literal: This approximates antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 宜體至意，勿復有請。」

translations.literal: You should embody my utmost intent and make no further requests."
translations.idiomatic: You should respect my intent and make no further requests.

sentences.zh: 於是大臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great ministers did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the chief ministers did not dare speak further.

sentences.zh: 蓋三年之制，斷自帝心，執政近臣皆主易月之說。

translations.literal: For the three-year regulation was decided by the emperor's own heart; the ruling chief ministers all upheld the doctrine of substituting months.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year regulation was decided by the emperor's own resolve, while the ruling chief ministers all upheld month substitution.

sentences.zh: 諫官謝鍔、禮官尤袤心知其不可，而不敢盡言。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Xie E and ritual official You Mao knew in their hearts it was wrong but did not dare speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Xie E and ritual official You Mao knew in their hearts it was wrong but did not dare speak fully.

sentences.zh: 惟敕令所刪定官沈清臣再上書：「願堅'主聽大事於內殿'之旨，將來祔廟畢日，預降御筆，截然示以終喪之志，杜絕輔臣方來之章，勿令再有奏請，力全聖孝，以示百官，以刑四海。」

translations.literal: Only Shen Qingchen, revising official of the Edict Office, again submitted a memorial: "I wish to uphold the intent of 'mainly hearing great affairs in the inner hall'; when the day of future enshrinement in the temple is completed, let an imperial brush edict be issued in advance, clearly showing the resolve of full mourning, cutting off future memorials from chief ministers, not permitting further requests, striving to complete sacred filial piety, to display it to the hundred officials and model it for the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Only Shen Qingchen, revising official of the Edict Office, again memorialized: "I wish to uphold the intent of 'mainly hearing great affairs in the inner hall'; when enshrinement is completed, let an imperial brush edict be issued in advance, clearly showing the resolve of full mourning, cutting off future memorials from chief ministers, permitting no further requests, striving to complete sacred filial piety, to display it to all officials and model it for the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝納用焉。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted and used it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this advice.

sentences.zh: 仍詔：「欑宮遵遺誥務從儉約，凡修營百費，並從內庫，毋侵有司經常之費。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued: "The encoffining palace should follow the testamentary instructions and strive for thrift; all construction expenses shall come from the inner treasury and must not encroach on the regular expenses of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued: "The encoffining palace should follow the testamentary instructions and strive for thrift; all construction expenses shall come from the inner treasury and must not encroach on the regular budgets of responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 諸路監司、州軍府監止進慰表，其餘禮並免，不得以進奉欑宮為名，有所貢獻。」

translations.literal: Supervisory commissioners of all circuits, prefectures, armies, and prefectural offices should submit only condolence memorials; all other rites are exempted; contributions must not be made in the name of presenting offerings to the encoffining palace."
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory commissioners of all circuits and prefectural offices should submit only condolence memorials; all other rites are exempted; no contributions may be made in the name of presenting offerings to the encoffining palace.

sentences.zh: 上陵名曰永思。

translations.literal: The mausoleum was named Yongsi.
translations.idiomatic: The tomb was named Yongsi.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年六月九日，孝宗崩。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Xiaozong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the sixth month in the fifth year of Shaoxi, Xiaozong died.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后有旨，皇帝以疾聽在內成服，太皇太后代皇帝行禮。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager issued an order: because the emperor was ill, he was permitted to assume mourning dress within; the grand empress dowager performed the rites on the emperor's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager ordered that because the emperor was ill, he was permitted to assume mourning dress within while the grand empress dowager performed the rites on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年六月九日，大祥。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the sixth month of the second year of Qingyuan, greater mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the sixth month in the second year of Qingyuan, greater mourning was observed.

sentences.zh: 八月十六日，禫祭。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the eighth month, the chan sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the eighth month the chan sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 時光宗不能執喪，甯宗嗣服，欲大祥畢更服兩月，曰：「但欲禮制全盡，不較此兩月。」

translations.literal: At the time Guangzong could not carry out mourning; Ningzong succeeded in mourning dress and wished after greater mourning was concluded to wear mourning two months longer, saying: "I only wish the ritual system to be fully complete; I do not quibble over these two months."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guangzong could not carry out mourning; Ningzong succeeded in mourning dress and wished after greater mourning to wear mourning two months longer, saying: "I only wish the ritual system to be fully complete; I do not quibble over these two months.

sentences.zh: 於是監察御史胡紘言：「孫為祖服，已過期矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Censor Hu Hong stated: "Mourning by a grandson for a grandfather has already passed its term.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Hu Hong stated: "Mourning by a grandson for a grandfather has already passed its term.

sentences.zh: 議者欲更持禫兩月，不知用何典禮？

translations.literal: Those deliberating wish to observe chan two months longer—by what ceremonial code is this?
translations.idiomatic: Those deliberating wish to observe chan two months longer—by what ceremonial code?

sentences.zh: 若曰嫡孫承重，則太上聖躬亦已康復，于宮中自行二十七月之重服，而陛下又行之，是喪有二孤也。

translations.literal: If one says the eldest grandson bears the weight, then the Supreme Emperor's sacred person has also recovered; he is himself practicing the heavy mourning of twenty-seven months within the palace, and Your Majesty practices it again—this is two solitary mourners in one mourning.
translations.idiomatic: If one says the eldest grandson bears the weight, then the Supreme Emperor has also recovered and is himself practicing twenty-seven months of heavy mourning within the palace, while Your Majesty practices it again—this makes two chief mourners in one funeral.

sentences.zh: 自古孫為祖服，何嘗有此禮？

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when has mourning by a grandson for a grandfather ever had such a ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when has mourning by a grandson for a grandfather ever had such a ritual?

sentences.zh: 詔侍從、台諫、給舍集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attendant officials, remonstrance officials, and drafting masters of the Secretariat to assemble deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered attendant officials, remonstrance officials, and drafting masters to assemble deliberations.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書葉翥等言：「孝宗升遐之初，太上聖體違豫，就宮中行三年之喪。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Ye Xu and others stated: "When Xiaozong first ascended on high, the Supreme Emperor's sacred body was unwell; he practiced three-year mourning within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Ye Xu and others stated: "When Xiaozong first died, the Supreme Emperor was unwell and practiced three-year mourning within the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受禪，正宜仿古方喪之服以為服，昨來有司失於討論。

translations.literal: The emperor received the abdication; he should properly follow ancient square-mourning dress as his mourning dress; yesterday the responsible offices failed in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the abdication and should properly follow ancient square-mourning dress; the responsible offices had failed in their deliberation.

sentences.zh: 今胡紘所奏，引古據經，別嫌明微，委為允當。

translations.literal: Hu Hong's present memorial cites antiquity and relies on the classics, distinguishes suspicion and clarifies subtlety—it is truly fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hong's present memorial cites antiquity and relies on the classics, distinguishes suspicion and clarifies subtle points—it is truly fitting.

sentences.zh: 欲從所請，參以典故：六月六日，大祥禮畢，皇帝及百官並純吉服；

translations.literal: We wish to follow the request, consulting precedents: on the sixth day of the sixth month, when greater mourning rites are concluded, the emperor and hundred officials shall all wear fully auspicious dress;
translations.idiomatic: We wish to follow the request, consulting precedents: on the sixth day of the sixth month, when greater mourning rites are concluded, the emperor and all officials shall wear fully auspicious dress;

sentences.zh: 七月一日，皇帝御正殿，饗祖廟。

translations.literal: on the first day of the seventh month, the emperor attends the main hall and feasts at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: on the first day of the seventh month, the emperor attends the main hall and feasts at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 將來禫祭，令禮官檢照累朝禮例施行。」

translations.literal: For the future chan sacrifice, order ritual officials to examine and follow accumulated dynastic ritual precedents."
translations.idiomatic: For the future chan sacrifice, order ritual officials to examine and follow accumulated dynastic ritual precedents.

sentences.zh: 四月庚戌，詔：「群臣所議雖合禮經，然於朕追慕之意，有所未安，早來奏知太皇太后，面奉聖旨，以太上皇帝雖未康愈，宮中亦行三年之制，宜從所議。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the fourth month, an edict stated: "Although the ministers' deliberation accords with the ritual classics, as to my intent of longing in remembrance, I am somewhat uneasy; I reported early to the grand empress dowager and received her sacred directive face to face: although the Supreme Emperor has not fully recovered, within the palace the three-year regulation is also practiced—the deliberation should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the fourth month, an edict stated: "Although the ministers' deliberation accords with the ritual classics, I am somewhat uneasy regarding my longing in remembrance; I reported early to the grand empress dowager and received her directive face to face: although the Supreme Emperor has not fully recovered, the palace also practices the three-year regulation—the deliberation should be followed.

sentences.zh: 朕躬奉慈訓，敢不遵依。」

translations.literal: I personally received her kindly instruction—how dare I not follow and comply."
translations.idiomatic: I personally received her kindly instruction—how dare I not comply."

sentences.zh: 初，高宗之喪，孝宗為三年服。

translations.literal: Initially, at Gaozong's mourning, Xiaozong wore three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, at Gaozong's mourning, Xiaozong wore three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 及孝宗之喪，有司請于易月之外，用漆紗淺黃之制，蓋循紹興以前之舊。

translations.literal: At Xiaozong's mourning, the responsible offices requested, beyond substituting months, using lacquered gauze pale yellow regulations—following the old practice before Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozong's mourning, responsible offices requested, beyond month substitution, lacquered gauze pale yellow dress—following practice before Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 朱熹初至，不以為然，奏言：「今已往之失，不及追改，惟有將來啟欑發引，禮當復用初喪之服，則其變除之節，尚有可議。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi first arrived, he did not consider this correct and memorialized: "Past errors cannot now be pursued and changed; only for the future opening of the encoffining hall and setting out of the procession should ritual return to initial mourning dress—then the nodes of change and removal may still be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi first arrived, he disagreed and memorialized: "Past errors cannot now be corrected; only for the future opening of the encoffining hall and funeral procession should ritual return to initial mourning dress—then the stages of change and removal may still be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 望明詔禮官稽考禮律，豫行指定。

translations.literal: I hope a clear edict will order ritual officials to examine ritual regulations and specify them in advance.
translations.idiomatic: I hope a clear edict will order ritual officials to examine ritual regulations and specify them in advance.

sentences.zh: 其官吏軍民方喪之服，亦宜稍為之制，勿使肆為華靡。」

translations.literal: As for the square-mourning dress of officials, soldiers, and commoners, regulations should also be made so they do not indulge in lavish ornament."
translations.idiomatic: Regulations should also be made for the square-mourning dress of officials, soldiers, and commoners so they do not indulge in lavish ornament.

sentences.zh: 其後，詔中外百官，皆以涼衫視事，蓋用此也。

translations.literal: Afterward, an edict ordered all officials within and without to conduct affairs in cool shirts—this was based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward an edict ordered all officials to conduct affairs in cool shirts—based on this recommendation.

sentences.zh: 方朱熹上議時，門人有疑者，未有以折之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi submitted this proposal, some among his disciples had doubts but had nothing with which to refute it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi submitted this proposal, some disciples had doubts but had nothing with which to refute it.

sentences.zh: 後讀《禮記正義·喪服小記》「為祖後者」條，因自識於本議之末，其略云：「准《五服年月格》，斬衰三年，嫡孫為祖謂承重者

translations.literal: Later, reading the Correct Meaning of the Book of Rites, "Mourning Dress, Small Record," entry "He Who Succeeds the Ancestor," he therefore appended a note at the end of his original proposal, stating in summary: "According to the Five Mourning Grades Years and Months Chart, severest grade three years—when the eldest grandson mourns for the grandfather, this is called bearing the weight
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading the Correct Meaning of the Book of Rites entry "He Who Succeeds the Ancestor" in the Small Record on Mourning Dress, he appended a note at the end of his original proposal, stating in summary: "According to the Five Mourning Grades Years and Months Chart, severest grade three years—when the eldest grandson mourns for the grandfather, this is called bearing the weight

sentences.zh: ，法意甚明，而《禮經》無文，但《傳》云：'父沒而為祖後者服斬。

translations.literal: , the intent of the law is very clear, yet the Ritual Classic has no text; only the Commentary says: 'When the father has died and one succeeds the ancestor, wear the severest grade.
translations.idiomatic: , the intent of the law is very clear, yet the Ritual Classic has no text; only the Commentary says: 'When the father has died and one succeeds the ancestor, wear the severest grade.

sentences.zh: '然而不見本經，未詳何據。

translations.literal: 'Yet this is not seen in the original classic; it is unclear on what basis.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is not seen in the original classic; the basis is unclear.

sentences.zh: 但《小記》云：'祖父沒而為祖母後者三年。

translations.literal: But the Small Record says: 'When the grandfather has died and one succeeds the grandmother, three years.
translations.idiomatic: But the Small Record says: 'When the grandfather has died and one succeeds the grandmother, three years.

sentences.zh: '可以傍照。

translations.literal: 'This may serve as collateral illumination.
translations.idiomatic: This may serve as collateral evidence.

sentences.zh: 至'為祖後者'條下疏中所引《鄭志》，乃有'諸侯父有廢疾不任國政，不任喪事'之問，而鄭答以'天子、諸侯之服皆斬'之文，方見父在而承國于祖服。

translations.literal: As for the Zheng Records cited in the commentary under the entry 'He Who Succeeds the Ancestor,' there is the question 'When a feudal lord's father has crippling illness and cannot bear state affairs or funeral affairs,' and Zheng answers with the text 'The Son of Heaven and feudal lords all wear the severest grade'—only then is it seen that while the father lives, one who inherits the state from the grandfather wears mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng Records cited in the commentary under 'He Who Succeeds the Ancestor' include the question 'When a feudal lord's father has crippling illness and cannot bear state or funeral affairs,' and Zheng answers with 'The Son of Heaven and feudal lords all wear the severest grade'—only then is it seen that while the father lives, one who inherits the state from the grandfather wears mourning.

sentences.zh: 向來上此奏時，無文字可檢，又無朋友可問，故大約且以禮律言之。

translations.literal: When I previously submitted this memorial, there was no text to examine and no friend to ask; therefore I spoke approximately from ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When I previously submitted this memorial, there was no text to examine and no friend to consult; therefore I spoke approximately from ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 亦有疑父在不當承重者，時無明白證驗，但以禮律人情大意答之，心常不安。

translations.literal: There was also doubt whether when the father lives one should not bear the weight; at the time there was no clear proof, and I answered only from the general intent of ritual regulations and human sentiment—my heart was often uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: I also doubted whether when the father lives one should not bear the weight; at the time there was no clear proof, and I answered only from the general intent of ritual regulations and human sentiment—my heart was often uneasy.

sentences.zh: 歸來稽考，始見此說，方得無疑。

translations.literal: Returning home and examining, I first saw this doctrine and then could be without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home and examining the texts, I first found this doctrine and then could be without doubt.

sentences.zh: 乃知學之不講，其害如此。

translations.literal: Thus I knew that when learning is not expounded, the harm is like this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I knew that when learning is not expounded, the harm is so great.

sentences.zh: 而《禮經》之文，誠有闕略，不無待于後人。

translations.literal: Yet the text of the Ritual Classic truly has omissions and gaps; it cannot but await later people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the text of the Ritual Classic truly has omissions and gaps and cannot but await later scholars.

sentences.zh: 向使無鄭康成，則此事終未有所斷決，不可直謂古經定制，一字不可增損也。」

translations.literal: If there had been no Zheng Xuan, this matter would ultimately never have been decided; one cannot simply say the ancient classic fixed the system and not a single character may be added or reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Had there been no Zheng Xuan, this matter would never have been decided; one cannot simply say the ancient classic fixed the system and not a single character may be added or removed.

sentences.zh: 已而詔於永思陵下宮之西，修奉欑宮，上陵名曰永阜。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered west of the lower palace of the Yongsi Mausoleum the building and tending of an encoffining palace; the mausoleum was named Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered construction west of the lower palace of the Yongsi Mausoleum of an encoffining palace; the tomb was named Yongfu.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年，光宗崩，上陵名曰永崇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan, Guangzong died; the mausoleum was named Yongchong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qingyuan, Guangzong died; the tomb was named Yongchong.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十七年，甯宗崩，上陵名曰永茂。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Jiading, Ningzong died; the mausoleum was named Yongmao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Jiading, Ningzong died; the tomb was named Yongmao.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，理宗崩，上陵名曰永穆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding, Lizong died; the mausoleum was named Yongmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingding, Lizong died; the tomb was named Yongmu.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳十年，度宗崩，上陵名曰永紹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun, Duzong died; the mausoleum was named Yongshao.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianchun, Duzong died; the tomb was named Yongshao.

sentences.zh: 自孝宗以降，外庭雖用易月之制，而宮中實行三年之喪雲。

translations.literal: From Xiaozong downward, although the outer court used the system of substituting months, within the palace three-year mourning was in fact practiced.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiaozong onward, although the outer court used month substitution, the inner palace in fact practiced three-year mourning.
